title: Why We Like the Foods We Like (SOP86)

sentences.en: Welcome to Speaking of Psychology, a bi-weekly podcast from the American Psychological Association.
sentences.zh: 欢迎收听《心理学谈话》，这是美国心理学会推出的一档双周播客。

sentences.en: I'm your host, Caitlin Luna.
sentences.zh: 我是主持人凯特琳·卢纳。

sentences.en: Why do some people scarf down anchovies by the pound while others recoil at the thought of a tuna fish sandwich?
sentences.zh: 为什么有些人能大口大口地吃凤尾鱼，而另一些人一想到金枪鱼三明治就退避三舍？

sentences.en: Why do the textures of certain foods like mushrooms turn people off?
sentences.zh: 为什么蘑菇等某些食物的质地会让人们感到反感？

sentences.en: Not only is taste a biologically complex experience, it is quite psychological.
sentences.zh: 味觉不仅是一种生物学上的复杂体验，它还相当具有心理学色彩。

sentences.en: Our guest for this episode is psychologist Dr. Linda Bardashuk, an international leader in taste research who is the Bushnell professor of food science and human nutrition at the
sentences.zh: 本期节目的嘉宾是心理学家琳达·巴达舒克博士，她是味觉研究领域的国际领军人物，也是佛罗里达大学食品科学与人类营养学系的布什内尔教授，以及该校

sentences.en: University of Florida and director for the psychophysical research at the University
sentences.zh: 嗅觉与味觉中心

sentences.en: Center for Smell and Taste.
sentences.zh: 心理物理学研究的主任。

sentences.en: She's known for her discovery of super tasters, people who have more taste buds than the average
sentences.zh: 她因发现“超级味觉者”（即味蕾数量多于常人的人）而闻名，

sentences.en: person, her work on enhancing the flavor of tomatoes, and for discovering a condition known as burning mouth syndrome.
sentences.zh: 她在提升番茄风味方面的工作，以及发现了一种被称为“口腔灼烧综合征”的疾病，都让她声名卓著。

sentences.en: Dr. Bardashuk is joining us via Skype from the University of Florida.
sentences.zh: 巴达舒克博士现在正通过Skype从佛罗里达大学与我们连线。

sentences.en: Welcome.
sentences.zh: 欢迎您。

sentences.en: Hi.
sentences.zh: 你好。

sentences.en: So, it may be surprising to people that taste is as psychological as it is biological.
sentences.zh: 那么，人们可能会感到惊讶，味觉既是生物学上的，也是心理学上的。

sentences.en: Can you explain how taste is studied from a psychological perspective?
sentences.zh: 您能解释一下如何从心理学角度研究味觉吗？

sentences.en: Well, taste is both biology and experience, and it's psychological because of the learning that we do.
sentences.zh: 嗯，味觉既是生物学体验，也是一种经历，而它之所以具有心理学色彩，是因为我们从中进行的学习。

sentences.en: We learn to like things.
sentences.zh: 我们通过学习来喜欢某些事物。

sentences.en: Some of our liking or disliking is built into the brain, but most of it is learned.
sentences.zh: 我们的一些喜好是与生俱来的，但大部分是后天习得的。

sentences.en: Does that explain why some people like very polarizing foods like Vegemite, durians, those really stinky cheeses?
sentences.zh: 这能解释为什么有些人喜欢像维吉麦酱、榴莲、那些臭气熏天的奶酪等极具争议的食物吗？

sentences.en: Is that genetic, cultural, or is it based on personal preference?
sentences.zh: 这是遗传的、文化的，还是基于个人偏好？

sentences.en: A lot of that is early experience.
sentences.zh: 很大程度上源于早期的经历。

sentences.en: They learn to like it very early.
sentences.zh: 他们很早就学会了喜欢这些东西。

sentences.en: Their culture promotes it.
sentences.zh: 他们的文化推崇这些食物。

sentences.en: They learned it from their parents.
sentences.zh: 他们是从父母那里学来的。

sentences.en: And what we learn to like when we experience it very early in life sticks with us.
sentences.zh: 而且，我们在生命早期体验并学会喜欢的东西，会伴随我们一生。

sentences.en: Mm-hmm.
sentences.zh: 嗯，确实。

sentences.en: And so, what if you hated, say, broccoli growing up, but now all of a sudden as an adult, you can't get enough?
sentences.zh: 那么，如果你小时候讨厌西兰花，但成年后突然又爱不释手了，这该怎么解释？

sentences.en: Are there changes in the taste psychology over time?
sentences.zh: 味觉心理会随着时间推移而改变吗？

sentences.en: The changes over time, some of it's biological.
sentences.zh: 随着时间推移产生的变化，部分是生物学上的。

sentences.en: Again, there are changes with aging.
sentences.zh: 同样，随着年龄增长，味觉也会发生变化。

sentences.en: But most of it is just the experience you accumulate.
sentences.zh: 但大部分变化只是你积累的经验。

sentences.en: And probably you didn't switch from disliking broccoli to liking it a lot.
sentences.zh: 而且你可能并不是从讨厌西兰花一下子转变为非常喜欢它。

sentences.en: It was probably gradual.
sentences.zh: 这很可能是循序渐进的。

sentences.en: And it probably happened because you paired broccoli with a lot of things you did like.
sentences.zh: 而且这很可能是因为你把西兰花和你真正喜欢的许多东西搭配在一起吃了。

sentences.en: And so, you learned it almost accidentally as you were eating things you liked a lot.
sentences.zh: 所以，你在吃自己非常喜欢的食物时，几乎是无意中学会了喜欢它。

sentences.en: And so, what causes certain food textures to bother people?
sentences.zh: 那么，是什么导致某些食物的质地会让人们感到困扰呢？

sentences.en: You know, for example, I like bananas, but sometimes the texture just makes me want to gag.
sentences.zh: 比如，我喜欢香蕉，但有时它的质地简直让我反胃。

sentences.en: No, texture is interesting.
sentences.zh: 不，质地问题很有趣。

sentences.en: In fact, if you lecture to students and you mention texture and you say they're texture some people don't like, you can actually watch people's faces get red in the audience.
sentences.zh: 事实上，如果你给学生讲课时提到质地，并说出某些人不喜欢的那种质地，你甚至能看到台下听众的脸变红。

sentences.en: It's embarrassing.
sentences.zh: 这很尴尬。

sentences.en: It's emotional.
sentences.zh: 这是一种情绪反应。

sentences.en: And we don't understand that very well.
sentences.zh: 而我们对此还了解得不够透彻。

sentences.en: For example, you know the little curly thing next to an egg yolk?
sentences.zh: 比如，你知道蛋黄旁边那个小小的卷曲的东西吗？

sentences.en: I can't stand that.
sentences.zh: 我受不了那个。

sentences.en: If I get that with my egg, I don't want to eat the rest of it.
sentences.zh: 如果我的鸡蛋里有那个东西，我就不想吃剩下的部分了。

sentences.en: And I don't generally admit that because people think it's a little weird.
sentences.zh: 我通常不会承认这一点，因为人们会觉得这有点奇怪。

sentences.en: Texture aversions are considered rather strange.
sentences.zh: 对质地的厌恶被认为相当古怪。

sentences.en: We don't talk about them much.
sentences.zh: 我们很少谈论它们。

sentences.en: But they are quite common, though, you said, right?
sentences.zh: 但正如您所说，它们其实很常见，对吧？

sentences.en: They're very common.
sentences.zh: 它们非常普遍。

sentences.en: And why is really a puzzle?
sentences.zh: 至于原因，确实是个谜。

sentences.en: Because they don't really have nutritional consequences.
sentences.zh: 因为它们并没有真正的营养后果。

sentences.en: So, something else is going on.
sentences.zh: 所以，肯定还有其他因素在起作用。

sentences.en: And that is something that hasn't been studied much.
sentences.zh: 而这一点还没有被深入研究过。

sentences.en: I'd really like to know more about it myself.
sentences.zh: 我自己也非常想了解更多。

sentences.en: Many of us probably have that person in our lives who only likes, or maybe we are that person, who only likes brown food or white food.
sentences.zh: 我们生活中可能都有这样的人，或者我们自己就是这样的人：只喜欢棕色食物或白色食物。

sentences.en: So, that's pasta, potatoes, chicken, or whatever.
sentences.zh: 比如意大利面、土豆、鸡肉之类的。

sentences.en: So, what causes people to be picky eaters?
sentences.zh: 那么，是什么导致人们变得挑食呢？

sentences.en: Wow.
sentences.zh: 哇。

sentences.en: Picky eaters is really a loaded subject, especially with parents.
sentences.zh: 挑食确实是一个沉重的话题，尤其是对家长而言。

sentences.en: Occasionally, I have a parent or grandparent bring a child to me because they're upset because the kid is a picky eater.
sentences.zh: 偶尔会有家长或祖父母带孩子来找我，因为他们对孩子挑食感到苦恼。

sentences.en: And they think the kid must be a super taster, and that explains it.
sentences.zh: 他们认为孩子一定是“超级味觉者”，并以此来解释这种行为。

sentences.en: So, they come to me in the hopes that I can verify that there's something going on.
sentences.zh: 所以他们来找我，希望我能证实这背后有什么原因。

sentences.en: The truth is we're all picky eaters to start with.
sentences.zh: 事实是，我们一开始都是挑食者。

sentences.en: We learn to accept things.
sentences.zh: 我们是学会接受事物的。

sentences.en: But if you look at the way we acquire preferences from the time we're babies, for example, vegetables are really, really slow to develop preference for.
sentences.zh: 但如果你观察我们从婴儿时期开始培养偏好的方式，比如蔬菜，对它们的偏好形成得非常非常缓慢。

sentences.en: And one of the reasons is you don't get much immediate reward from a vegetable.
sentences.zh: 原因之一是你从蔬菜中得不到多少即时的奖励。

sentences.en: Things that have fat in them, you get an immediate calorie load.
sentences.zh: 含有脂肪的食物能让你获得即时的热量补充。

sentences.en: Things that are sweet or salty, you've got hardwired liking built into your brain.
sentences.zh: 甜味或咸味的食物，你的大脑中天生就设定了对它们的喜爱。

sentences.en: But vegetables don't buy you much.
sentences.zh: 但蔬菜给不了你太多好处。

sentences.en: So, we really are acquiring our liking for foods, one food at a time, except for sweet and salty, which we like as soon as we can perceive them.
sentences.zh: 所以，我们确实是在一点一点地培养对食物的喜爱，除了甜味和咸味——我们一能感知到它们就喜欢上了。

sentences.en: And that learning liking just takes time.
sentences.zh: 而这种对喜好的学习是需要时间的。

sentences.en: Now, why do some people develop such dislikes?
sentences.zh: 那么，为什么有些人会产生如此强烈的厌恶感呢？

sentences.en: That's actually a wonderful question.
sentences.zh: 这真是一个绝佳的问题。

sentences.en: And part of it can do with gastrointestinal illness.
sentences.zh: 部分原因可能与胃肠道疾病有关。

sentences.en: For example, if a small child tends to get nauseated frequently and throw up, anything that you eat when you're experiencing nausea is likely to be learned as disgusting very, very
sentences.zh: 例如，如果一个小孩经常感到恶心并呕吐，那么你在感到恶心时吃的任何东西，都很容易被大脑迅速地

sentences.en: quickly.
sentences.zh: 标记为令人作呕。

sentences.en: It's one trial learning.
sentences.zh: 这是一种“一次性学习”。

sentences.en: So, sometimes people have aversions to a lot of foods because they got sick a lot as a baby.
sentences.zh: 所以，有时人们对很多食物产生厌恶，是因为他们小时候经常生病。

sentences.en: When you don't have that kind of history or can't remember it, sometimes it can be very puzzling to explain.
sentences.zh: 当你没有那样的经历或者记不清时，有时很难解释原因。

sentences.en: But I'll tell you one thing don't do.
sentences.zh: 但我可以告诉你一件事：千万别这样做。

sentences.en: If you've got a picky kid, don't bug them about it.
sentences.zh: 如果你有一个挑食的孩子，不要为此去烦他们。

sentences.en: Don't insist they eat things they don't like.
sentences.zh: 不要强迫他们吃他们不喜欢的食物。

sentences.en: And don't make a big fuss about it because you're going to create a problem that you're then really going to require professional help to solve.
sentences.zh: 也不要为此大惊小怪，因为你会制造出一个问题，到时候真的需要专业帮助才能解决。

sentences.en: So, if you do want to get a picky eater to eat more vegetables or fruit, let's say, but might be difficult, is there a way you can try to,
sentences.zh: 那么，如果你想让一个挑食者多吃蔬菜或水果，这可能很困难，有没有什么方法可以尝试，

sentences.en: instead of forcing them to eat something
sentences.zh: 而不是强迫他们吃某种东西，

sentences.en: like that, find a way to show them how good it can taste or hide vegetables or fruit in other foods?
sentences.zh: 而是找到一种方法向他们展示这些食物有多美味，或者把蔬菜水果藏在其他食物里？

sentences.en: Is that possible?
sentences.zh: 这可能吗？

sentences.en: You know, one of the best ways to get a kid to try something new to eat is to have another kid at the table, eat it.
sentences.zh: 你知道，让孩子尝试新食物的最好方法之一，就是让餐桌上的另一个孩子吃给他们看。

sentences.en: Now, when that's not practical, there is another solution.
sentences.zh: 如果这不切实际，还有另一个解决方案。

sentences.en: For example, you want a kid to eat broccoli, serve it with something good on it, like sprinkle a little sugar on it, put something fat on it, add butter to it, add cheese.
sentences.zh: 例如，你想让孩子吃西兰花，就在上面加点好吃的，比如撒点糖，加点脂肪，加点黄油，或者加点奶酪。

sentences.en: The beauty is that our learning theorist experts tell us that the kid will acquire a preference
sentences.zh: 妙处在于，我们的学习理论专家告诉我们，孩子会培养出

sentences.en: for the flavor of the broccoli because it's paired with something that's really highly liked.
sentences.zh: 对西兰花风味的偏好，因为它与他们非常喜欢的食物搭配在一起了。

sentences.en: Later on, when you take that highly liked substance away, the flavor preferences remain.
sentences.zh: 之后，当你把那种他们非常喜欢的物质拿走时，对风味的偏好依然存在。

sentences.en: So, you can actually condition a preference to something like the flavor of broccoli by adding sugar to it.
sentences.zh: 所以，你确实可以通过加糖来调节对西兰花风味的偏好。

sentences.en: And later, when you take the sugar away, you still have the broccoli preference.
sentences.zh: 后来，当你把糖拿走时，你依然保留了对西兰花的偏好。

sentences.en: It must be an interesting taste to have some sugar on your broccoli, right?
sentences.zh: 在西兰花上撒糖，这味道一定很特别，对吧？

sentences.en: Well, you know, dieticians tend to be very bothered by instructions like this.
sentences.zh: 嗯，你知道，营养学家往往对这样的指导感到非常困扰。

sentences.en: But sugar is not the evil that we tend to make it out to be.
sentences.zh: 但糖并不是我们通常认为的那种恶魔。

sentences.en: We evolved with sugar.
sentences.zh: 我们是在糖的陪伴下进化而来的。

sentences.en: Frankly, artificial sweeteners worry me a lot more.
sentences.zh: 坦白说，人工甜味剂更让我担心。

sentences.en: How come?
sentences.zh: 为什么这么说？

sentences.en: Why do you think they're so much worse than regular sugar?
sentences.zh: 你为什么认为它们比普通糖糟糕得多？

sentences.en: Well, first of all, they have a lot of toxicities associated with them.
sentences.zh: 嗯，首先，它们伴随着很多毒性问题。

sentences.en: It concerns me that we tend not to pay attention to some of the literature about this.
sentences.zh: 让我担忧的是，我们往往不关注关于这方面的文献。

sentences.en: For example, cyclamate was taken off the American market because it was found to be carcinogenic.
sentences.zh: 例如，甜蜜素被美国市场下架，因为它被发现具有致癌性。

sentences.en: Well, it turns out that probably wasn't correct.
sentences.zh: 嗯，事实证明这可能并不准确。

sentences.en: But saccharin is known to be mildly carcinogenic.
sentences.zh: 但糖精被认为是轻微致癌的。

sentences.en: And there it stays.
sentences.zh: 可它依然存在。

sentences.en: Because at the time, people tried to get it off the diet.
sentences.zh: 因为当时人们试图把它从饮食中剔除。

sentences.en: It was about the only artificial sweetener out there.
sentences.zh: 那是当时市面上唯一的人工甜味剂。

sentences.en: And people who thought they needed artificial sweeteners really raised a row about it.
sentences.zh: 而那些认为自己需要人工甜味剂的人对此大吵大闹。

sentences.en: So it's probably almost better if you can, I mean, unless you're diabetic or some other physical need, to have regular sugar on your food.
sentences.zh: 所以，如果你能做到的话——除非你是糖尿病患者或有其他身体需求——吃普通糖可能更好。

sentences.en: Just don't have a lot of it.
sentences.zh: 只是不要吃太多。

sentences.en: Be careful about the quantities you eat.
sentences.zh: 注意你摄入的量。

sentences.en: But a certain amount of sugar is really not a bad thing.
sentences.zh: 但适量的糖其实并不是坏事。

sentences.en: You're right.
sentences.zh: 你说得对。

sentences.en: If you're a diabetic, then you have to worry about it.
sentences.zh: 如果你是糖尿病患者，那你就必须担心这个问题。

sentences.en: This is one of the reasons that I'm interested, very much interested in research that might lead us to a sweetener that really is safe.
sentences.zh: 这也是我非常关注那些可能引导我们找到真正安全甜味剂的研究的原因之一。

sentences.en: But I'm happy to tell you we're doing that right now.
sentences.zh: 但我很高兴地告诉你，我们现在正在做这件事。

sentences.en: We're working on volatiles.
sentences.zh: 我们正在研究挥发性物质。

sentences.en: Now, a volatile for people who aren't trained in chemistry, it's a compound that can be in gaseous form.
sentences.zh: 对于没有受过化学训练的人来说，挥发性物质是一种可以以气态形式存在的化合物。

sentences.en: Like you sniff something, a flower, the compounds that you're smelling are volatiles.
sentences.zh: 就像你闻花香一样，你闻到的那些化合物就是挥发性物质。

sentences.en: They're in gaseous form.
sentences.zh: 它们以气态形式存在。

sentences.en: The compounds that we sniff when we smell a fruit and are so pleasant, those are volatiles.
sentences.zh: 当我们闻水果时所嗅到的那些令人愉悦的化合物，就是挥发性物质。

sentences.en: Now, those compounds, when you bite into that fruit, those compounds actually go in your mouth and they rise at the back of your mouth through a space up to the back of your nose.
sentences.zh: 现在，当你咬一口水果时，这些化合物实际上会进入你的口腔，并从口腔后部上升，穿过一个空间到达鼻腔后部。

sentences.en: Think about post-nasal drip.
sentences.zh: 想想鼻后滴漏。

sentences.en: That space that the post-nasal drip comes through is what volatiles rise through.
sentences.zh: 鼻后滴漏流经的那个空间，就是挥发性物质上升的通道。

sentences.en: And so a volatile, you can bite in and the odorant, a volatile, can rise at the back of your mouth and go into your nose from the rear.
sentences.zh: 所以，当你咬下一口食物，挥发性物质（气味分子）可以从口腔后部上升，从后方进入你的鼻子。

sentences.en: Now, when your brain detects a volatile coming in that path, it sends it to a part of the brain that also handles taste and the two interact there.
sentences.zh: 当你的大脑检测到挥发性物质通过这条路径进入时，它会将其发送到大脑中同样处理味觉的区域，两者在那里相互作用。

sentences.en: And there are some volatiles that actually intensify the taste message.
sentences.zh: 有些挥发性物质实际上会增强味觉信息。

sentences.en: That's fascinating.
sentences.zh: 这太迷人了。

sentences.en: And you, we raised a lot of really interesting points that I want to address in a couple different questions here.
sentences.zh: 你提出了很多非常有趣的问题，我想在接下来的几个问题中一一解答。

sentences.en: But just to wrap up the section about picky eaters, you know, why are some people more adventurous than others?
sentences.zh: 但关于挑食者这一节，我想总结一下：为什么有些人比其他人更具冒险精神？

sentences.en: On the flip side of being a picky eater.
sentences.zh: 也就是挑食者的反面。

sentences.en: Well, first of all, being adventurous is one more general characteristic of personality.
sentences.zh: 嗯，首先，具有冒险精神是一种更普遍的人格特征。

sentences.en: And I honestly don't know what makes us more adventurous.
sentences.zh: 老实说，我不知道是什么让我们变得更具冒险精神。

sentences.en: But if you want to become more adventurous in food, you have to go out and try new foods.
sentences.zh: 但如果你想在饮食上变得更具冒险精神，你就必须走出去尝试新食物。

sentences.en: This is something that I run into when I see a patient who's got taste damage and they can't taste things as well as they used to.
sentences.zh: 当我遇到味觉受损、无法像以前那样品尝食物的病人时，我经常会遇到这种情况。

sentences.en: I urge them to go out and try a lot of new things.
sentences.zh: 我敦促他们走出去尝试很多新东西。

sentences.en: And part of that is in the hope that they're going to find a few sensory inputs that are still going to be really good.
sentences.zh: 部分原因是希望他们能找到一些仍然感觉非常好的感官输入。

sentences.en: But there's a hidden purpose to that.
sentences.zh: 但其中还有一个隐藏的目的。

sentences.en: And the hidden purpose is the more things you try, the more things you give your brain an opportunity to learn to like.
sentences.zh: 这个隐藏的目的就是：你尝试的东西越多，你给大脑学习喜欢它们的机会就越多。

sentences.en: You eat something and the sensory signature of that, actually, the retronasal olfaction, that message I was telling you that comes up the rear of the mouth,
sentences.zh: 当你吃东西时，它的感官特征——实际上是鼻后嗅觉，也就是我刚才告诉你的那种从口腔后部上升的信息，

sentences.en: that is the signature of the food, the flavor of it.
sentences.zh: 那就是食物的特征，也就是它的风味。

sentences.en: Your brain records that.
sentences.zh: 你的大脑会记录下这一点。

sentences.en: And if that flavor is coming into the brain at the same time calories are coming in through your stomach, your brain is going to tell you to like that flavor.
sentences.zh: 如果这种风味进入大脑的同时，热量也通过胃部进入，你的大脑就会告诉你去喜欢这种风味。

sentences.en: So the more different things you eat, the more unusual flavors you are pairing with calories and your brain is going to make you like them.
sentences.zh: 所以你尝试的食物种类越多，你将越多的独特风味与热量联系起来，你的大脑就会让你喜欢上它们。

sentences.en: That's fascinating.
sentences.zh: 这太迷人了。

sentences.en: So there are ways to enhance what you like to eat just to give it a shot and try and see if you can like it again.
sentences.zh: 所以，确实有方法可以增强你对食物的喜爱，只要给它一个机会，试着看看你是否能重新喜欢上它们。

sentences.en: Okay.
sentences.zh: 好的。

sentences.en: That's really interesting.
sentences.zh: 这真的很有趣。

sentences.en: The more you explore the food world, the more things you're going to learn to like.
sentences.zh: 你对美食世界探索得越多，你就会学着喜欢上越多的东西。

sentences.en: Now, you have to be careful because if you start out really disliking a lot of things, you can then expose yourself to things you don't like.
sentences.zh: 不过，你得小心，因为如果你一开始就非常排斥很多东西，你可能会让自己接触到那些你不喜欢的事物。

sentences.en: And sometimes it'll backfire and you'll get to like it even less.
sentences.zh: 有时这会适得其反，让你变得更不喜欢它们。

sentences.en: So it's better to start off neutral and pair something with calories or a good taste like sweet or salty and your brain will make you like it.
sentences.zh: 所以，最好保持中立，将某种食物与热量或甜、咸等好味道搭配在一起，你的大脑就会让你喜欢上它。

sentences.en: And we've talked about smell a little bit.
sentences.zh: 我们之前稍微聊过嗅觉。

sentences.en: So can you talk about how integral smell is the full sensory experience of food?
sentences.zh: 那么，你能谈谈嗅觉对于完整的食物感官体验有多重要吗？

sentences.en: So, you know, anyone who's ever had a cold, which is probably everyone who's listening, can attest to how bland and basically terrible food tastes when they're sick.
sentences.zh: 你知道，任何感冒过的人——可能在听节目的每个人都感冒过——都能证明，生病时食物尝起来是多么平淡，简直糟糕透顶。

sentences.en: Well, I mean, that's actually a myth.
sentences.zh: 嗯，其实那是个误区。

sentences.en: The notion that you can't perceive the flavor of food when you've got a cold,
sentences.zh: 关于感冒时无法感知食物风味的说法，

sentences.en: there are some people that do lose the ability to smell because the area that the odorants have to go through to get to receptors gets swollen from a cold.
sentences.zh: 确实有些人会失去嗅觉，因为感冒导致气味分子到达受体所经过的区域肿胀了。

sentences.en: And the odors just don't get through the area.
sentences.zh: 气味分子无法通过那个区域。

sentences.en: But that's not true for most people.
sentences.zh: 但这对大多数人来说并非如此。

sentences.en: For example, I don't lose the sense of smell at all when I get a cold.
sentences.zh: 例如，我感冒时一点嗅觉都不会丧失。

sentences.en: And I think most people don't.
sentences.zh: 我想大多数人也是这样。

sentences.en: But unfortunately, there is a fairly rare condition where the virus itself can damage the olfactory system.
sentences.zh: 但不幸的是，确实存在一种相当罕见的情况，病毒本身会损害嗅觉系统。

sentences.en: And those people do lose smell with a cold, but it outlasts the cold.
sentences.zh: 这些人感冒时确实会失去嗅觉，而且这种状况会持续到感冒痊愈之后。

sentences.en: Oh, OK.
sentences.zh: 哦，好的。

sentences.en: But just smell in general, how is it, how integral is it to the two enjoying and tasting your food?
sentences.zh: 但就嗅觉而言，它对于享受和品尝食物到底有多重要？

sentences.en: It's extremely important.
sentences.zh: 它极其重要。

sentences.en: And let me first distinguish between taste and smell, because I think it's easier to understand all this if you really get that distinction.
sentences.zh: 首先让我区分一下“味觉”和“嗅觉”，因为如果你真正理解了这个区别，理解这一切会更容易。

sentences.en: Taste is what's coming from your tongue.
sentences.zh: 味觉来自于你的舌头。

sentences.en: Sweet, salty, sour, bitter, umami.
sentences.zh: 甜、咸、酸、苦、鲜。

sentences.en: If you buy the advertising stuff coming from places like Kajinomoto, which I do not.
sentences.zh: 如果你相信像味之素（Kajinomoto）这类公司宣传的那样——我个人是不信的。

sentences.en: But the four basic tastes, sweet, salty, sour, bitter coming from your tongue.
sentences.zh: 但基本的四种味觉——甜、咸、酸、苦——是来自于你的舌头。

sentences.en: Now, when you sniff with your nose, you're bringing volatiles, odorants in through your nose.
sentences.zh: 当你用鼻子吸气时，你把挥发性物质、气味分子通过鼻子带了进来。

sentences.en: They have to go through a very small opening.
sentences.zh: 它们必须穿过一个非常小的开口。

sentences.en: And that opening is what gets swollen during the cold for some people.
sentences.zh: 而那个开口就是有些人感冒时会肿胀的地方。

sentences.en: But once the volatile goes through that opening, it hits the receptors and sends a message to the brain.
sentences.zh: 但一旦挥发性物质穿过那个开口，它就会触碰到受体并向大脑发送信号。

sentences.en: And that's smell.
sentences.zh: 那就是嗅觉。

sentences.en: That's what we sniff from the outside world.
sentences.zh: 那是我们从外界吸入的东西。

sentences.en: But the nose has a second job.
sentences.zh: 但鼻子还有第二个工作。

sentences.en: And that second job is you put food in your mouth.
sentences.zh: 第二个工作是当你把食物放进嘴里时进行的。

sentences.en: You bite into it.
sentences.zh: 你咬它。

sentences.en: You chew it.
sentences.zh: 你咀嚼它。

sentences.en: You swallow it.
sentences.zh: 你吞咽它。

sentences.en: And swallowing forces those volatiles up that passage at the back of the mouth that I mentioned.
sentences.zh: 吞咽动作会迫使那些挥发性物质通过我提到的口腔后部的通道向上移动。

sentences.en: Now, that input is going up and it's hitting, going through the same small opening, going to the receptors.
sentences.zh: 现在，这些输入信息向上移动，穿过同一个小开口，到达受体。

sentences.en: So you've got a molecule that you could sniff and it comes into your nose one way.
sentences.zh: 所以，同一种分子，你可以通过鼻子从外部吸入。

sentences.en: And that same molecule can go through a different pathway if you get it from your mouth.
sentences.zh: 而同样的分子，如果你从口腔摄入，它会走一条不同的路径。

sentences.en: But the brain pays attention to the difference and it sends the input to different places in the brain.
sentences.zh: 但大脑会注意到这种差异，并将输入信息发送到大脑的不同区域。

sentences.en: So when you sniff, the input goes to one area and we call it smell.
sentences.zh: 所以当你吸气时，输入信息进入一个区域，我们称之为嗅觉。

sentences.en: Now, you put food in your mouth, chew it, swallow it, and that odorous input goes to another part of the brain.
sentences.zh: 而当你把食物放进嘴里、咀嚼、吞咽时，那些气味输入会进入大脑的另一个部分。

sentences.en: And actually, that input is what produces flavor.
sentences.zh: 实际上，正是这种输入产生了“风味”。

sentences.en: And flavor is going to the same part of the brain as taste and they can interact.
sentences.zh: 风味会进入与味觉相同的大脑区域，它们可以相互作用。

sentences.en: That was what I was mentioning earlier.
sentences.zh: 这就是我之前提到的。

sentences.en: Now, here's the key thing.
sentences.zh: 现在，关键点来了。

sentences.en: We are hardwired.
sentences.zh: 我们是天生设定好的。

sentences.en: Our brains are wired to make us like sweet, sour.
sentences.zh: 我们的大脑被设定为让我们喜欢甜味、酸味。

sentences.en: Well, not sour so much for most people, but sweet, salty, and to dislike bitter.
sentences.zh: 嗯，对大多数人来说酸味没那么明显，但甜味、咸味是喜欢的，而苦味是排斥的。

sentences.en: That's hardwired.
sentences.zh: 这是天生的。

sentences.en: But liking smells is entirely learned in humans.
sentences.zh: 但对气味的喜好在人类身上完全是后天习得的。

sentences.en: At least that's what we think so far.
sentences.zh: 至少目前我们是这么认为的。

sentences.en: If there are any smells that we're born loving, we haven't identified them yet.
sentences.zh: 如果有什么气味是我们天生就喜欢的，我们还没发现。

sentences.en: Well, that's fascinating.
sentences.zh: 嗯，这太迷人了。

sentences.en: So put this together for food.
sentences.zh: 那么把这些结合到食物上来看。

sentences.en: You've got taste, which is giving you hardwired affect, plus or minus.
sentences.zh: 你有味觉，它给你提供天生的情感反应，正向或负向。

sentences.en: And you've got smell, which is giving you learned affect.
sentences.zh: 你还有嗅觉，它给你提供习得的情感反应。

sentences.en: And that depends very much and almost entirely, in fact, on your experience.
sentences.zh: 这在很大程度上，甚至几乎完全取决于你的经验。

sentences.en: Put it together and you've got food.
sentences.zh: 把它们合在一起，你就得到了食物。

sentences.en: It's complicated.
sentences.zh: 这很复杂。

sentences.en: Yes, it's very complex.
sentences.zh: 是的，非常复杂。

sentences.en: And also smell and taste is known to evoke powerful memories.
sentences.zh: 而且嗅觉和味觉也被认为能唤起强烈的记忆。

sentences.en: So can you explain how that works as well?
sentences.zh: 你能解释一下这是怎么运作的吗？

sentences.en: Not taste.
sentences.zh: 不是味觉。

sentences.en: Oh, not taste.
sentences.zh: 哦，不是味觉。

sentences.en: It's smell that produces those memories.
sentences.zh: 是嗅觉产生了那些记忆。

sentences.en: We call it the Proust effect because Proust wrote about his madeleines with tea in his, I think, aunt's kitchen.
sentences.zh: 我们称之为“普鲁斯特效应”，因为普鲁斯特在他的作品中写到了他在——我想是他姑妈的厨房里——吃玛德琳蛋糕配茶的情景。

sentences.en: And they brought back all these evocative memories.
sentences.zh: 它们带回了所有这些令人回味的记忆。

sentences.en: So yes, we associate emotion with smell very, very powerfully.
sentences.zh: 所以是的，我们将情感与嗅觉非常、非常强烈地联系在一起。

sentences.en: And in fact, it may be the most important phenomenon, and maybe with the exception of being
sentences.zh: 事实上，这可能是最重要的现象，也许除了能够通过嗅觉识别食物之外，

sentences.en: able to identify food by smell, but having affective reactions to it controls a huge amount of our food behavior.
sentences.zh: 但对食物产生情感反应控制了我们大量的饮食行为。

sentences.en: And going back to speaking about food in itself, you know, why do some foods like say fish sauce
sentences.zh: 回到谈论食物本身，你知道，为什么有些食物，比如鱼露

sentences.en: or anchovies, like I mentioned, so on their own, most people don't like, or many people don't like, but if they're added to something, they suddenly become delicious.
sentences.zh: 或者我提到的凤尾鱼，单独吃时大多数人不喜欢，或者很多人不喜欢，但如果把它们加到别的东西里，它们突然就变得美味了？

sentences.en: So like in Vietnamese food, a fish sauce really enhances the flavors or an anchovies in a Caesar dressing can really make it taste really good.
sentences.zh: 比如在越南菜中，鱼露真的能提升风味，或者凯撒沙拉酱里的凤尾鱼真的能让它尝起来非常好吃。

sentences.en: Can you explain how that works?
sentences.zh: 你能解释一下这是怎么运作的吗？

sentences.en: Yeah, a lot of it's simple concentration.
sentences.zh: 是的，很大程度上是因为简单的浓度问题。

sentences.en: That is, when you taste pure fish sauce, you're really getting a full dose.
sentences.zh: 也就是说，当你品尝纯鱼露时，你实际上是在摄入足量的剂量。

sentences.en: When you add it to food, it's both diluted by the food and it's diluted by the other sensory experience.
sentences.zh: 当你把它加到食物中时，它既被食物稀释了，也被其他感官体验稀释了。

sentences.en: That is, when you put a whole bunch of tastes and smells together, they suppress each other.
sentences.zh: 也就是说，当你把一大堆味道和气味放在一起时，它们会相互抑制。

sentences.en: And what you end up with is an experience that is certainly not the linear sum of all the things that went into it.
sentences.zh: 最终你得到的是一种体验，它肯定不是所有成分的线性总和。

sentences.en: For example, imagine when you make a beautiful Chinese sauce to have on dumplings, you add soy sauce, maybe you add, if you really love salt, salt, sugar, a little vinegar, you put
sentences.zh: 例如，想象一下当你制作一种美味的中式饺子蘸酱时，你加入酱油，如果你特别喜欢咸味，可能还会加盐、糖、一点醋，你把

sentences.en: all that together.
sentences.zh: 所有这些加在一起。

sentences.en: And if you added those tastes and smells linearly, it would knock the top of your head off.
sentences.zh: 如果你是线性地叠加这些味道和气味，那味道会让你受不了。

sentences.en: So they suppress each other.
sentences.zh: 所以它们会相互抑制。

sentences.en: So what happens when you eat food is it's all kept within a reasonable intensity domain.
sentences.zh: 因此，当你吃东西时，一切都保持在一个合理的强度范围内。

sentences.en: So it's really those chemicals reacting together and working together that make them taste really good once they're all mixed.
sentences.zh: 所以，正是这些化学物质混合在一起并共同作用，才让它们在混合后尝起来非常美味。

sentences.en: Absolutely.
sentences.zh: 绝对是这样。

sentences.en: And also, you learn the mixture sensation.
sentences.zh: 而且，你还会学习这种混合的感觉。

sentences.en: That is one of the beautiful things our brains do is to record information about what we've eaten before.
sentences.zh: 我们大脑所做的美妙事情之一，就是记录我们以前吃过什么的信息。

sentences.en: And those are saved almost as like templates in the brain.
sentences.zh: 这些信息几乎像模板一样保存在大脑中。

sentences.en: So for example, look at bacon.
sentences.zh: 例如，看看培根。

sentences.en: You eat bacon.
sentences.zh: 你吃培根。

sentences.en: It's got protein in it.
sentences.zh: 它含有蛋白质。

sentences.en: It's got fat in it.
sentences.zh: 它含有脂肪。

sentences.en: Those are two things that your brain perceives as really good.
sentences.zh: 这两样东西你的大脑都认为是非常好的。

sentences.en: So it's going to make you love the flavor that comes in with bacon.
sentences.zh: 所以它会让你爱上培根带来的那种风味。

sentences.en: Now, that flavor is actually a composite.
sentences.zh: 现在，那种风味实际上是一个复合体。

sentences.en: It's a lot of salt.
sentences.zh: 它有很多盐分。

sentences.en: It's a variety.
sentences.zh: 它有很多种类。

sentences.en: I mean, dozens of different volatiles make up the smell and the flavor of bacon.
sentences.zh: 我是说，几十种不同的挥发性物质构成了培根的气味和风味。

sentences.en: You put those all together and they produce a template, a certain sensory signature that's stored in your brain.
sentences.zh: 你把它们放在一起，它们就产生了一个模板，一种存储在你大脑中的特定感官特征。

sentences.en: And the next time you eat bacon, you're going to recognize it very quickly.
sentences.zh: 下次你再吃培根时，你很快就能认出它来。

sentences.en: And people go wild for bacon these days, it seems like.
sentences.zh: 而且现在人们似乎对培根非常疯狂。

sentences.en: Well, look what it's got in it.
sentences.zh: 嗯，看看它里面有什么。

sentences.en: Fat protein, what's not to like?
sentences.zh: 脂肪、蛋白质，有什么理由不喜欢呢？

sentences.en: Exactly.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: Add a little sugar, maybe from pancakes or something, maple syrup.
sentences.zh: 加一点糖，也许来自煎饼之类的，枫糖浆。

sentences.en: Dangerous combination.
sentences.zh: 危险的组合。

sentences.en: And why do some people, can they tell, why can some people tolerate super spicy foods?
sentences.zh: 还有，为什么有些人，他们能分辨吗，为什么有些人能忍受超辣的食物？

sentences.en: Like they can add the hottest hot sauce to their chili and love it or eat these ghost peppers and all sorts of things like that.
sentences.zh: 比如他们可以在辣椒酱里加最辣的辣酱并乐在其中，或者吃这些鬼椒之类的各种东西。

sentences.en: But while other people can't even stand a hint of heat, that's like some of my family members are like that.
sentences.zh: 但有些人甚至连一点点辣味都受不了，我的一些家人就是这样。

sentences.en: No heat at all on their food.
sentences.zh: 他们的食物里一点辣味都不能有。

sentences.en: Why is, why can some people eat really hot food and others can't?
sentences.zh: 为什么，为什么有些人能吃很辣的食物而另一些人不能？

sentences.en: Some of it's genetic.
sentences.zh: 部分原因是遗传。

sentences.en: For example, taste buds in your tongue are surrounded by a basket of pain fibers.
sentences.zh: 例如，你舌头上的味蕾周围环绕着一束痛觉纤维。

sentences.en: So the more taste buds you've got, the more pain your tongue is capable of perceiving.
sentences.zh: 所以你的味蕾越多，你的舌头能感知的疼痛就越多。

sentences.en: Now, the number of taste buds you're born with is under genetic control, at least in part.
sentences.zh: 现在，你天生拥有的味蕾数量至少在一定程度上受遗传控制。

sentences.en: There may be several factors.
sentences.zh: 可能还有其他几个因素。

sentences.en: So if you're born with a lot of taste buds, we call those people super tasters.
sentences.zh: 所以如果你天生味蕾很多，我们称这些人是“超级味觉者”。

sentences.en: You're also born with a very large number of pain fibers.
sentences.zh: 你天生也拥有大量的痛觉纤维。

sentences.en: And so you're going to feel the burn of a pepper about three times as much.
sentences.zh: 所以你会感觉到辣椒的灼烧感比别人强烈三倍左右。

sentences.en: And I was, I love watching the food channel and you watch these pepper eating contests.
sentences.zh: 我喜欢看美食频道，你会看到这些吃辣椒比赛。

sentences.en: The person who can eat that really powerful pepper, there are two factors.
sentences.zh: 那个能吃下那种强力辣椒的人，有两个因素。

sentences.en: One of them is they're probably not a super taster.
sentences.zh: 其中之一是他们可能不是超级味觉者。

sentences.en: So they don't have the biology to perceive the pain as intense.
sentences.zh: 所以他们没有那种能感知强烈疼痛的生理结构。

sentences.en: But in addition, capsaicin is the compound that makes all chili peppers burn.
sentences.zh: 但此外，辣椒素是让所有辣椒产生灼烧感的化合物。

sentences.en: And capsaicin desensitizes pain receptors.
sentences.zh: 而辣椒素会使痛觉受体脱敏。

sentences.en: So if you habitually eat chili pepper, you're desensitizing the pain receptors on your tongue.
sentences.zh: 所以如果你习惯吃辣椒，你就是在让舌头上的痛觉受体脱敏。

sentences.en: If you'd like to prove that to yourself, go for a vacation.
sentences.zh: 如果你想向自己证明这一点，去度个假吧。

sentences.en: Go for two weeks or so without eating any chili pepper.
sentences.zh: 去两周左右不吃任何辣椒。

sentences.en: Then come back and eat the amount you're used to eating.
sentences.zh: 然后回来吃你习惯吃的量。

sentences.en: It will burn.
sentences.zh: 它会让你感到灼烧。

sentences.en: And that relates to your taste buds regenerating over time, correct?
sentences.zh: 这和你的味蕾随时间再生有关，对吧？

sentences.en: No, there's no, regeneration is a natural part of the taste system.
sentences.zh: 不，不是的，再生是味觉系统的自然组成部分。

sentences.en: And all of our taste buds die off and regenerate.
sentences.zh: 我们所有的味蕾都会死亡并再生。

sentences.en: They don't even have a very long taste life.
sentences.zh: 它们的寿命甚至不是很长。

sentences.en: And burn doesn't actually damage anything.
sentences.zh: 而且灼烧感实际上并不会造成任何损害。

sentences.en: I mean, it produces a powerful sensation of burn.
sentences.zh: 我是说，它产生了一种强烈的灼烧感。

sentences.en: But for the most part, things like capsaicin and chili peppers do not actually produce any damage.
sentences.zh: 但在大多数情况下，辣椒素和辣椒实际上并不会造成任何伤害。

sentences.en: But you said you just become desensitized to them over time.
sentences.zh: 但你刚才说你只是随着时间推移对它们脱敏了。

sentences.en: Yeah, you don't feel the burn.
sentences.zh: 是的，你感觉不到那种灼烧感了。

sentences.en: And that is really fun.
sentences.zh: 这真的很有趣。

sentences.en: For example, suppose you go to a restaurant and you order a hot dish and it's too hot for you.
sentences.zh: 例如，假设你去一家餐馆点了一道辣菜，但对你来说太辣了。

sentences.en: Fill your mouth with it.
sentences.zh: 让你的嘴里充满它。

sentences.en: Really let the burn hit a maximum.
sentences.zh: 真正让灼烧感达到最大值。

sentences.en: And then sit and chat for a few minutes.
sentences.zh: 然后坐下来聊几分钟。

sentences.en: You can drink ice water to keep the burn down while you're doing that.
sentences.zh: 你可以喝冰水来缓解灼烧感，同时做这些事。

sentences.en: And the burn will naturally fade away in 10, 15 minutes.
sentences.zh: 灼烧感会在10到15分钟内自然消失。

sentences.en: At the end of that fade, put the hot food back in your mouth and it won't burn as much.
sentences.zh: 在那种感觉消退后，把热食放回嘴里，就不会那么烫了。

sentences.en: You can desensitize your pain receptors on your tongue that faSt.
sentences.zh: 你可以这么快就让舌头上的痛觉感受器脱敏。

sentences.en: Wow, that is fascinating.
sentences.zh: 哇，这太神奇了。

sentences.en: I thought it would be like a gradual process, but it can be over the course of one meal.
sentences.zh: 我原以为这是一个渐进的过程，没想到一顿饭的时间就能完成。

sentences.en: Nope, it can happen really in minutes.
sentences.zh: 不，这确实可以在几分钟内发生。

sentences.en: And speaking of the super tasters you just mentioned, so those are people with more taste buds.
sentences.zh: 说到你刚才提到的“超级味觉者”，他们是指那些拥有更多味蕾的人。

sentences.en: And while this sounds like a blessing in some ways, you've also found that that may not be the case.
sentences.zh: 虽然这听起来在某些方面是一种天赋，但你发现事实可能并非如此。

sentences.en: So can you explain why?
sentences.zh: 你能解释一下原因吗？

sentences.en: Well, in terms of eating food, there's one thing about being a super taster that really is wonderful.
sentences.zh: 嗯，就吃东西而言，成为超级味觉者确实有一点非常棒。

sentences.en: We discovered this fairly recently.
sentences.zh: 我们是最近才发现这一点的。

sentences.en: That is the pleasure you get from your favorite foods is more intense if you're a super taster.
sentences.zh: 那就是如果你是超级味觉者，你从最喜欢的食物中获得的快感会更强烈。

sentences.en: Now, we don't know why that is.
sentences.zh: 目前我们还不知道原因。

sentences.en: This is why I think there's more to being a super taster than just taste buds because pleasure is happening in the brain.
sentences.zh: 这就是为什么我认为成为超级味觉者不仅仅是因为味蕾，因为快感是在大脑中产生的。

sentences.en: So something in the brain is different with super tasters and they're getting more pleasure from their favorite foods.
sentences.zh: 所以超级味觉者的大脑中有些不同，他们从自己喜欢的食物中获得了更多的快感。

sentences.en: Now, that isn't the blessing, you might think, because the super tasters don't have quite as many favorite foods.
sentences.zh: 不过，你可能觉得这算不上什么福气，因为超级味觉者喜欢的食物并没有那么多。

sentences.en: There are also a lot of things they don't like to eat.
sentences.zh: 他们也有很多不喜欢吃的东西。

sentences.en: They tend to be pickier eaters because they're very sensitive to bitter, for example, and they don't like certain texture.
sentences.zh: 他们往往更挑食，因为他们对苦味非常敏感，而且不喜欢某些口感。

sentences.en: Now, that's a case of where texture – there is a certain amount of biology in it, and texture is more intense to super tasters, so they can be put off by it.
sentences.zh: 这就是口感的问题——其中包含一定的生物学因素，口感对超级味觉者来说更强烈，所以他们可能会因此感到反感。

sentences.en: Yeah, and so for those super tasters, they may not be likely to eat some bitter things.
sentences.zh: 没错，对于那些超级味觉者来说，他们可能不太愿意吃一些苦的东西。

sentences.en: Maybe they're not eating some of those cruciferous vegetables like Brussels sprouts and those things that are really good.
sentences.zh: 也许他们不吃那些十字花科蔬菜，比如抱子甘蓝之类的，而这些东西其实非常好。

sentences.en: That can be very good for you, by the way.
sentences.zh: 顺便说一句，这对你的健康非常有益。

sentences.en: So that's the second piece of this.
sentences.zh: 所以这是第二部分。

sentences.en: Your diet involves risk factors for diseases, and one of the reasons we're very interested in the fact that there are super tasters is that their diets are affected.
sentences.zh: 你的饮食涉及疾病的风险因素，我们对“超级味觉者”这一事实非常感兴趣的原因之一，就是他们的饮食受到了影响。

sentences.en: They don't choose to eat the same foods.
sentences.zh: 他们不会选择吃同样的食物。

sentences.en: And because of that, it changes their risk factors.
sentences.zh: 正因如此，这改变了他们的风险因素。

sentences.en: So, for example, colon cancer, one of the risk factors is fiber in your diet.
sentences.zh: 例如，结肠癌的风险因素之一就是饮食中的纤维摄入量。

sentences.en: Well, super tasters don't like eating highly textured foods as much as others.
sentences.zh: 超级味觉者不像其他人那样喜欢吃口感强烈的食物。

sentences.en: They eat fewer of them, and so they actually are at a slightly higher biological risk for colon cancer.
sentences.zh: 他们吃得较少，因此他们在生物学上患结肠癌的风险实际上略高一些。

sentences.en: Now, that's a small difference, but it's big enough that you can actually see it.
sentences.zh: 虽然差异很小，但大到足以被观察出来。

sentences.en: We did a study, for example, looking at colon polyps.
sentences.zh: 例如，我们做了一项关于结肠息肉的研究。

sentences.en: Colon polyps are a risk factor for colon cancer, and they're produced in people who don't consume enough fiber.
sentences.zh: 结肠息肉是结肠癌的风险因素，多见于纤维摄入不足的人群。

sentences.en: And if you look, in fact, at super tasters and people who are not super tasters, they have a different number of colon polyps.
sentences.zh: 事实上，如果你观察超级味觉者和非超级味觉者，会发现他们结肠息肉的数量不同。

sentences.en: The super tasters have more.
sentences.zh: 超级味觉者的息肉更多。

sentences.en: Switch to something else, like head and neck cancer.
sentences.zh: 换个话题，比如头颈癌。

sentences.en: Now, the risk factors are consumption of alcohol and smoking.
sentences.zh: 其风险因素是饮酒和吸烟。

sentences.en: And super tasters don't drink as much alcohol.
sentences.zh: 而超级味觉者喝的酒没那么多。

sentences.en: They don't like it because it burns their tongues and doesn't taste very good.
sentences.zh: 他们不喜欢喝酒，因为酒精会灼烧他们的舌头，而且味道也不好。

sentences.en: And they also don't like to smoke for reasons, sensory reasons as well.
sentences.zh: 而且出于各种原因，包括感官方面的原因，他们也不喜欢抽烟。

sentences.en: So the super tasters is an advantage when you look at head and neck cancer.
sentences.zh: 所以，在看待头颈癌时，成为“超级味觉者”反而是一种优势。

sentences.en: And is this, is there a genetic component to being a super tasters?
sentences.zh: 那么，成为“超级味觉者”有遗传因素吗？

sentences.en: There is.
sentences.zh: 有的。

sentences.en: We don't know how big it is.
sentences.zh: 我们还不知道具体影响有多大。

sentences.en: Nobody's done a family study on it yet, but it certainly is genetic.
sentences.zh: 目前还没有人对此进行过家族研究，但它确实是遗传性的。

sentences.en: For example, if you look at the tongues of identical twins, they're going to look very, very similar.
sentences.zh: 例如，如果你观察同卵双胞胎的舌头，你会发现它们看起来非常非常相似。

sentences.en: And by the way, you can look at the tongue and see whether somebody is a super taster.
sentences.zh: 顺便说一下，你可以通过观察舌头来判断一个人是否是“超级味觉者”。

sentences.en: And your listeners can do this with, by going to the supermarket and buying blue food coloring.
sentences.zh: 听众朋友们可以亲自试一试，去超市买点蓝色食用色素就行。

sentences.en: Bring it home, swab it on your tongue with a Q-tip, and swallow a couple of times to move the dye around.
sentences.zh: 带回家，用棉签蘸取涂在舌头上，然后吞咽几次让色素分布均匀。

sentences.en: Look at your tongue.
sentences.zh: 观察一下你的舌头。

sentences.en: Best to do it in a magnifying mirror with a flashlight.
sentences.zh: 最好在放大镜前用手电筒照着看。

sentences.en: And what you'll see are pink circles against the blue background.
sentences.zh: 你会看到蓝色背景上有粉色的小圆圈。

sentences.en: Those pink circles are fungiform papillae.
sentences.zh: 那些粉色的小圆圈就是菌状乳头。

sentences.en: They're structures that hold taste buds.
sentences.zh: 它们是容纳味蕾的结构。

sentences.en: And you'll see that some people have a huge number of them.
sentences.zh: 你会发现有些人拥有极多数量的菌状乳头。

sentences.en: Their tongues look like they're absolutely tiled with these pink circles.
sentences.zh: 他们的舌头上几乎密密麻麻地铺满了这些粉色圆圈。

sentences.en: And then there are others like me.
sentences.zh: 而像我这样的人则不同。

sentences.en: I'm not a super taster.
sentences.zh: 我不是“超级味觉者”。

sentences.en: And for me, those pink circles are like polka dots.
sentences.zh: 对我来说，那些粉色圆圈就像是波点图案一样。

sentences.en: There's a lot of space between them.
sentences.zh: 它们之间有很大的空隙。

sentences.en: So you can see by looking at the tongue whether you're really an extreme super taster or not.
sentences.zh: 所以，通过观察舌头，你可以看出自己是否属于极端的“超级味觉者”。

sentences.en: You can't really see it.
sentences.zh: 其实你看不出太细微的差别。

sentences.en: Most people are in the middle.
sentences.zh: 大多数人处于中间水平。

sentences.en: But you can see it with the extremes.
sentences.zh: 但对于极端情况，你是可以看出来的。

sentences.en: That sounds like a fun experiment to do at home.
sentences.zh: 听起来这是一个很有趣的居家实验。

sentences.en: Oh, it's wonderful.
sentences.zh: 噢，这非常棒。

sentences.en: Kids love this, by the way, for science projects.
sentences.zh: 顺便提一下，孩子们很喜欢把它当作科学项目来做。

sentences.en: Yeah, that's a great idea.
sentences.zh: 是啊，这真是个好主意。

sentences.en: And how would being a super taster relate to weight?
sentences.zh: 那么，“超级味觉者”的身份与体重有什么关系吗？

sentences.en: I mean, you talked about and possibly obesity or being overweight.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，你之前提到过它可能与肥胖或超重有关。

sentences.en: You talked about maybe being a risk factor for not consuming enough fiber.
sentences.zh: 你还提到过，这可能是导致纤维摄入不足的一个风险因素。

sentences.en: But could it also relate to someone maybe being more overweight or obese because they might not be eating some of these healthier foods that aren't as tasty?
sentences.zh: 但它是否也可能与某人超重或肥胖有关，因为他们可能不吃那些不太好吃的健康食品？

sentences.en: Wouldn't you think so?
sentences.zh: 你不觉得是这样吗？

sentences.en: We thought so early on.
sentences.zh: 我们起初也是这么认为的。

sentences.en: But in fact, obesity is not really connected with super tasting.
sentences.zh: 但事实上，肥胖与“超级味觉”并没有真正的关联。

sentences.en: If you look at weight differences, you can find some groups of people where there might be a slight weight difference.
sentences.zh: 如果你观察体重差异，确实能发现某些群体之间可能存在轻微的体重差异。

sentences.en: And when there is, usually the super tasters are thinner.
sentences.zh: 而当存在差异时，通常“超级味觉者”反而更瘦一些。

sentences.en: But it's not a very big effect.
sentences.zh: 但它的影响并不是很大。

sentences.en: Okay, that's interesting.
sentences.zh: 好的，这很有意思。

sentences.en: I want to also touch on a point you mentioned a little while ago when you're talking about getting food poisoning or getting sick on some food, maybe as a baby.
sentences.zh: 我还想谈谈你刚才提到的一个观点，关于食物中毒或因某种食物而生病，也许是在婴儿时期。

sentences.en: But, you know, this can happen throughout your life.
sentences.zh: 但你要知道，这种情况可能发生在你的一生中。

sentences.en: So say you got food poisoning from some food and you feel like you can never eat it again.
sentences.zh: 假设你因为某种食物中毒了，感觉自己再也无法吃那种食物了。

sentences.en: Is there any way to overcome that?
sentences.zh: 有什么办法能克服吗？

sentences.en: It's hard.
sentences.zh: 很难。

sentences.en: Without making yourself sick?
sentences.zh: 在不让自己难受的情况下？

sentences.en: It's hard.
sentences.zh: 很难。

sentences.en: It's one trial learning.
sentences.zh: 这属于一次性习得。

sentences.en: But consider, for example, a cancer patient who is going to get radiation therapy or chemotherapy.
sentences.zh: 但试想一下，比如一位即将接受放疗或化疗的癌症患者。

sentences.en: And some of these therapies make you nauseated.
sentences.zh: 其中一些疗法会让你感到恶心。

sentences.en: So that nausea is going to condition onto foods and make a lot of foods become disgusting.
sentences.zh: 所以这种恶心感会与食物产生条件反射，让很多食物变得令人作呕。

sentences.en: So picture the cancer patient surviving cancer, going home, hoping to eat his or her favorite meal, biting into it and finding it disgusting.
sentences.zh: 试想一下，癌症患者战胜了癌症，回到家，满心欢喜地想吃顿最爱的饭菜，结果咬上一口却发现它令人作呕。

sentences.en: This is rough.
sentences.zh: 这太难受了。

sentences.en: And one of my tasks in the clinical world is to talk to patients like this and explain that, in fact, this is the biology of food aversions.
sentences.zh: 我在临床工作中的任务之一，就是与这样的患者交谈，并向他们解释，事实上，这就是食物厌恶的生物学机制。

sentences.en: The way to get over such an aversion, it's a conditioning effect.
sentences.zh: 克服这种厌恶的方法，其实是一种条件反射的消退。

sentences.en: So you try to extinguish it.
sentences.zh: 所以你要尝试去消除它。

sentences.en: That is, try to eat the food that you've had trouble with when you're really feeling good.
sentences.zh: 也就是说，试着在你感觉状态非常好时，去吃那些让你感到困扰的食物。

sentences.en: And if you're lucky, and you repeat this a few times, you may be able to extinguish the aversion.
sentences.zh: 如果你足够幸运，并且重复几次，你或许就能消除这种厌恶感。

sentences.en: But I have to tell you, it's rugged.
sentences.zh: 但我得告诉你，这非常艰难。

sentences.en: I developed an aversion to maraschino cherries, sitting, eating them in the back of the car, driving to California on a vacation.
sentences.zh: 我曾经对红樱桃产生了厌恶，当时我坐在车后座吃着它们，正要去加州度假。

sentences.en: I was reading comic books and I was carsick.
sentences.zh: 我当时在看漫画书，结果晕车了。

sentences.en: That aversion is so powerful that I cannot eat those things today.
sentences.zh: 那种厌恶感太强烈了，以至于今天我都没法吃那种东西。

sentences.en: If I get one on a plate, I hope nobody's looking and I just shove it off the edge.
sentences.zh: 如果盘子里出现一颗，我希望没人看见，然后就会把它拨到一边去。

sentences.en: I don't even want to see it.
sentences.zh: 我甚至连看都不想看。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: So it's so tied into, like we were talking before about, you know, the smell and the whole experience is tied into your memories.
sentences.zh: 所以这和我们之前谈到的很像，气味和整个体验都与你的记忆紧密相连。

sentences.en: And if that nausea memory is so strong, it's very difficult to overcome that.
sentences.zh: 如果那种恶心的记忆太强烈，就很难克服它。

sentences.en: Very, very difficult.
sentences.zh: 非常、非常困难。

sentences.en: Is the same, does that same principle apply to say if you're trying to get yourself to like some food that you want to like,
sentences.zh: 同样的原则是否也适用于你想让自己喜欢某种食物，

sentences.en: but struggle with, whether that be, you know, mushrooms, Brussels sprouts, that sort of thing?
sentences.zh: 但却感到困难的情况？比如蘑菇、抱子甘蓝之类的东西？

sentences.en: Can you apply that same technique?
sentences.zh: 你能运用同样的技巧吗？

sentences.en: It's easier to learn to like a food than it is to get over an aversion.
sentences.zh: 学会喜欢一种食物比克服一种厌恶要容易得多。

sentences.en: That is, if you're completely neutral to something, as I said before, your best bet, first of all, simple exposure will help.
sentences.zh: 也就是说，如果你对某样东西完全没感觉，正如我之前所说，最好的办法首先就是简单的接触。

sentences.en: That is, just eat it a few times.
sentences.zh: 也就是多吃几次。

sentences.en: Don't eat a lot of it, but just eat it.
sentences.zh: 不用吃很多，只要吃就行。

sentences.en: You'll probably find yourself coming to like it.
sentences.zh: 你很可能会发现自己慢慢喜欢上它了。

sentences.en: But if you want to speed that up, like with a kid who's finicky, put something good on it.
sentences.zh: 但如果你想加快这个过程，比如针对挑食的孩子，可以在上面加点好吃的。

sentences.en: It's like we said with the broccoli, sprinkle a little sugar on, put some cheese on it.
sentences.zh: 就像我们说西兰花那样，撒点糖，或者加点奶酪。

sentences.en: It'll help.
sentences.zh: 会有帮助的。

sentences.en: And speaking of disgust, we kind of touched on that as well.
sentences.zh: 说到厌恶，我们之前也稍微提到了这一点。

sentences.en: Are there any foods that disgust nearly everybody?
sentences.zh: 有没有什么食物是几乎所有人都觉得恶心的？

sentences.en: I mean, I know that we've talked before about some of these foods that are cultural,
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，我知道我们之前讨论过一些带有文化色彩的食物，

sentences.en: something people had growing up like Vegemite or durians, but is there anything that's universally panned?
sentences.zh: 比如人们从小吃到大的维吉麦酱或榴莲，但有没有什么是全世界都排斥的？

sentences.en: You know, the person to ask about that is Paul Rosen.
sentences.zh: 关于这个问题，你应该去问保罗·罗森（Paul Rosen）。

sentences.en: He's the disgust expert.
sentences.zh: 他是厌恶感方面的专家。

sentences.en: And I think he has found that there are disgusting foods that are disgusting to a lot of people,
sentences.zh: 我想他发现确实有一些食物对很多人来说都是令人作呕的，

sentences.en: and they often have an animal origin, like feces or a decaying body, something like this.
sentences.zh: 而且它们通常源于动物，比如粪便或腐烂的尸体之类的东西。

sentences.en: So there are certain things that we do culturally tend to be really disgusted by.
sentences.zh: 所以确实有些东西在文化上让我们感到非常厌恶。

sentences.en: But then again, disgust is also learned by these conditioned aversions.
sentences.zh: 但话说回来，厌恶感也是通过这些条件反射习得的。

sentences.en: It's very easy to develop a disgust for something if you've eaten it and gotten sick.
sentences.zh: 如果你吃过某种东西并因此生病，就很容易对它产生厌恶感。

sentences.en: I did this to myself on purpose once.
sentences.zh: 我曾经故意对自己做过这种实验。

sentences.en: I was coming down with a flu, and I was nauseated.
sentences.zh: 当时我快要感冒了，感到很恶心。

sentences.en: I drove home, and I always go buy Kentucky Fried Chicken.
sentences.zh: 我开车回家，路上总是会去买肯德基。

sentences.en: So I stopped off and bought my favorite, all dark meat, extra crispy, and ate it while I was nauseated.
sentences.zh: 于是我停下车，买了最爱的全黑肉、超脆炸鸡，并在恶心的状态下把它吃了下去。

sentences.en: Now, I knew what I was doing, but I still developed the aversion.
sentences.zh: 虽然我知道自己在做什么，但我还是产生了厌恶感。

sentences.en: And it was very powerful.
sentences.zh: 而且这种感觉非常强烈。

sentences.en: For a while, I found myself not even driving by Kentucky Fried Chicken.
sentences.zh: 有一段时间，我甚至发现自己连肯德基都不敢路过。

sentences.en: And even now, if I want extra crispy, all dark meat, I buy it at Popeye's.
sentences.zh: 即使是现在，如果我想吃超脆的全黑肉炸鸡，我也会去大力水手炸鸡（Popeye's）买。

sentences.en: I don't go to Kentucky Fried Chicken.
sentences.zh: 我不会去肯德基。

sentences.en: So these aversions are powerful, and they take over.
sentences.zh: 所以这些厌恶感很强大，而且会占据主导地位。

sentences.en: And it's important to have some compassion for people who've experienced these.
sentences.zh: 对那些经历过这些的人保持同情是很重要的。

sentences.en: And this is one of the things I feel about people who have real food dislikes.
sentences.zh: 这也是我对那些真正有食物厌恶的人的看法。

sentences.en: It's not something to make fun of.
sentences.zh: 这不是什么值得嘲笑的事情。

sentences.en: It's something that produces real distress.
sentences.zh: 这会给人带来真正的痛苦。

sentences.en: And I really don't believe in giving kids a hard time if they don't want to eat something they find disgusting.
sentences.zh: 我真的不赞成因为孩子不想吃他们觉得恶心的东西就为难他们。

sentences.en: Yeah, you do raise a good point.
sentences.zh: 没错，你提到了一个很好的观点。

sentences.en: I mean, you said if some people are picky eaters for whatever reason,
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，你说如果有些人因为某种原因比较挑食，

sentences.en: it might be stressful for them to go into a situation like a party or a restaurant where they struggle to find something they like and don't want to also be singled out in the crowd for getting something,
sentences.zh: 那么进入聚会或餐厅这种场合对他们来说可能会有压力，因为他们很难找到自己喜欢的东西，也不想因为点了某种“无聊”的食物而在人群中显得格格不入。

sentences.en: quote unquote, boring.
sentences.zh: 所谓的“无聊”。

sentences.en: So, yeah, that's a good point, though, to be sensitive to that and try not to push people.
sentences.zh: 所以，是的，对此保持敏感并尽量不去强迫别人，这是一个很好的观点。

sentences.en: Because, like you said, it does have a stress component to it.
sentences.zh: 因为正如你所说，这确实包含压力因素。

sentences.en: By the way, a food anthropologist told me a wonderful excuse to make if you don't want to eat something.
sentences.zh: 顺便说一句，一位食物人类学家告诉我一个绝妙的借口，如果你不想吃某种东西，可以用这个理由。

sentences.en: Suggest you have an allergy to it or that that particular food is something that makes you sick.
sentences.zh: 你可以说你对它过敏，或者说那种特定的食物会让你生病。

sentences.en: Mostly that's a social explanation that works for people.
sentences.zh: 这主要是一个对人们行之有效的社会学解释。

sentences.en: And I actually have seen some children who turned out to be extreme supertasters.
sentences.zh: 而且我确实见过一些孩子，他们后来成了极端的“超级味觉者”。

sentences.en: And I took pictures of their tongues and gave them copies to take back to show their friends and told them that they've now heard from an expert that it's not healthy to eat foods you don't like.
sentences.zh: 我给他们的舌头拍了照，还打印出来让他们带回去给朋友看，并告诉他们，现在你们已经从专家那里听说，吃自己不喜欢的食物是不健康的。

sentences.en: That's a great idea.
sentences.zh: 这主意真棒。

sentences.en: It makes the kids feel a little better.
sentences.zh: 这会让孩子们感觉好受一些。

sentences.en: I love that.
sentences.zh: 我喜欢这个。

sentences.en: I'm not sure their parents agree, but I think it's important.
sentences.zh: 我不确定他们的父母是否同意，但我认为这很重要。

sentences.en: Yeah, I like that.
sentences.zh: 是啊，我也喜欢这样。

sentences.en: So, speaking of children, children seem to be more sensitive to food than adults.
sentences.zh: 那么，说到孩子，孩子们似乎比成年人对食物更敏感。

sentences.en: Is that true?
sentences.zh: 是真的吗？

sentences.en: And does taste change over a lifespan?
sentences.zh: 而且味觉会随着年龄增长而改变吗？

sentences.en: That's a wonderful question.
sentences.zh: 这是一个非常棒的问题。

sentences.en: The truth is we're all born neophobic.
sentences.zh: 事实是，我们天生就对新事物有恐惧感。

sentences.en: That means we're worried about anything new.
sentences.zh: 这意味着我们对任何新鲜事物都会感到担忧。

sentences.en: And that's a very important survival characteristic.
sentences.zh: 这是一种非常重要的生存特征。

sentences.en: You want to watch out for something you don't know anything about.
sentences.zh: 对于不了解的东西，你自然会想要保持警惕。

sentences.en: You don't want to eat it unless you've learned it's safe.
sentences.zh: 除非你确认它是安全的，否则你不会想去吃它。

sentences.en: Well, in our culture, we learn it's safe because our parents tell it.
sentences.zh: 嗯，在我们的文化中，我们通过父母的告知来学习什么是安全的。

sentences.en: You know, even animals do that.
sentences.zh: 你知道，甚至动物也会这样做。

sentences.en: For example, a rat pup will sniff its mother's mouth to tell what she's been eating.
sentences.zh: 例如，幼鼠会嗅它母亲的嘴，来判断她吃了什么。

sentences.en: And that rat pup is very likely to go off and eat the food that has the same smell.
sentences.zh: 而那只幼鼠很有可能会跑去吃同样气味的食物。

sentences.en: So, we socially teach people how to eat things that are safe.
sentences.zh: 所以，我们通过社会化方式教导人们如何食用安全的食物。

sentences.en: And culturally, we even label our food to make it safe.
sentences.zh: 在文化上，我们甚至会给食物贴上标签，使其显得安全。

sentences.en: That's what spices do for us.
sentences.zh: 这就是香料对我们的作用。

sentences.en: For example, typically, if you want to eat a food that reminds you of your homeland, if you're an immigrant, for example, you use the spices from home.
sentences.zh: 例如，通常情况下，如果你是移民，想吃一种让你想起家乡的食物，你会使用家乡的香料。

sentences.en: And you put those even on a novel food.
sentences.zh: 即使是在一种陌生的食物上，你也会放上这些香料。

sentences.en: And you can make that novel food seem like it belongs more to that culturally safe food you grew up with.
sentences.zh: 这样你就能让那种陌生的食物，看起来更像是你从小吃到大的那种文化上安全的食物。

sentences.en: Well, that's a great idea.
sentences.zh: 嗯，这真是个好主意。

sentences.en: I never thought about that, though.
sentences.zh: 不过我从来没想过这一点。

sentences.en: This is a learned behavior.
sentences.zh: 这是一种习得性行为。

sentences.en: I was also reading somewhere as I was researching this that babies in the womb might like, so for example, if the mother ate garlic,
sentences.zh: 我在研究这个课题时也读到过，胎儿在子宫里可能就会产生偏好，比如，如果母亲吃了大蒜，

sentences.en: the baby can tolerate garlic and breast milk after they're born because they were able to taste it in the amniotic fluid.
sentences.zh: 婴儿出生后就能接受大蒜和母乳的味道，因为他们在羊水中就已经尝过这种味道了。

sentences.en: You're talking about Julie Manella's work.
sentences.zh: 你指的是朱莉·曼内拉（Julie Manella）的研究。

sentences.en: That is brilliant research.
sentences.zh: 那是一项非常出色的研究。

sentences.en: Yes.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: Julie has shown that both volatiles that a baby can detect in amniotic fluid as well as in mother's milk will carry valence.
sentences.zh: 朱莉已经证明，婴儿在羊水和母乳中能探测到的挥发性物质都带有某种效价。

sentences.en: That is, if you get mom to eat something special like carrots when she's pregnant,
sentences.zh: 也就是说，如果你让妈妈在怀孕期间吃一些特别的东西，比如胡萝卜，

sentences.en: you may find that your newborn baby is more interested in eating carrots than if they never had the exposure.
sentences.zh: 你可能会发现，比起从未接触过这些味道的婴儿，你的新生儿对吃胡萝卜会更感兴趣。

sentences.en: So amniotic fluid in mother's milk are ways to get an organism to like foods, both other mammals and humans.
sentences.zh: 所以，羊水和母乳是让生物——无论是其他哺乳动物还是人类——喜欢上某种食物的途径。

sentences.en: Yeah, that's really interesting.
sentences.zh: 是啊，这真的很有趣。

sentences.en: I'm actually pregnant right now, and I've been eating a lot of carrots and garlic, so hopefully that bodes well for an adventurous eater in the future.
sentences.zh: 我目前正好怀孕了，我一直在吃很多胡萝卜和大蒜，希望这预示着未来会有一个不挑食的孩子。

sentences.en: We'll see.
sentences.zh: 我们拭目以待。

sentences.en: I guess I can keep you updated on that.
sentences.zh: 我想我可以随时向你汇报进展。

sentences.en: Does any specific gender have a better palate?
sentences.zh: 是否有特定的性别拥有更好的味觉？

sentences.en: I've heard anecdotally so that women have a better palate, so they're better at tasting wine and all the different notes you can get off a glass of wine.
sentences.zh: 我听说过一些轶事，说女性的味觉更好，所以她们更擅长品酒，能分辨出一杯酒中所有的细微差别。

sentences.en: Is that true?
sentences.zh: 这是真的吗？

sentences.en: There's some truth to that.
sentences.zh: 这确实有一定道理。

sentences.en: First of all, women have a more sensitive sense of taste, which is pretty fascinating.
sentences.zh: 首先，女性的味觉更敏锐，这非常迷人。

sentences.en: And if you consider the fact that what women eat affects a fetus, there's real biological wisdom to that.
sentences.zh: 如果你考虑到女性的饮食会影响胎儿这一事实，这其中有着真正的生物学智慧。

sentences.en: But more, remember that women, especially in our culture and actually most cultures, have more experience in the kitchen.
sentences.zh: 但更重要的是，请记住，女性，特别是在我们的文化中，实际上在大多数文化中，在厨房里的经验更丰富。

sentences.en: So they've learned more about smells in particular.
sentences.zh: 所以她们对气味的学习更多，尤其是对气味的辨别。

sentences.en: So having a woman be, say, a better wine taster probably has something to do with the fact she's learned to identify so many odors because she's had more exposure to them.
sentences.zh: 因此，女性成为更好的品酒师，可能与她们因为接触更多而学会了识别如此多气味这一事实有关。

sentences.en: Now, anybody can get that exposure, and this is what wine tasting is all about.
sentences.zh: 现在，任何人都可以获得这种接触，这就是品酒的全部意义所在。

sentences.en: If you learn to become a better wine taster,
sentences.zh: 如果你想成为一名更好的品酒师，

sentences.en: the way you learn that is you learn to recognize specific volatiles that are associated with the things that are likely to be found in wine.
sentences.zh: 学习的方法就是学会识别与葡萄酒中可能出现的物质相关的特定挥发性成分。

sentences.en: Yeah, that's the interesting part of that.
sentences.zh: 是啊，这正是其中有趣的部分。

sentences.en: I have a friend who's into wine, and he does some, you know, wine tastings for friends.
sentences.zh: 我有个朋友很喜欢葡萄酒，他会为朋友们举办一些品酒会。

sentences.en: And there's this wheel that talks about all the different tastes.
sentences.zh: 有一个轮盘图，上面列出了各种不同的味道。

sentences.en: And some of them can be amazing, like a fresh strawberry.
sentences.zh: 有些味道令人惊叹，比如新鲜草莓味。

sentences.en: Some of them can be downright disgusting, like cat urine that was on the wheel or rubber, you know, that kind of thing, that things you can taste in wine.
sentences.zh: 有些则简直令人作呕，比如轮盘上提到的猫尿味或橡胶味，你知道，就是那种你在酒里能尝到的味道。

sentences.en: And I just have what I've gotten through, you know, re-osmosis through the years is just that if you are into wine tasting, you want to sniff things like tobacco, leather, chalk,
sentences.zh: 我这些年来通过渗透学习到的就是，如果你喜欢品酒，你就得去闻烟草、皮革、粉笔之类的东西，

sentences.en: all these things so you can identify those flavors when you're sniffing the wine, when you're tasting it.
sentences.zh: 闻过所有这些东西，你才能在品酒或闻酒时识别出那些风味。

sentences.en: That's right.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: And that wine aroma wheel is Ann Nobles.
sentences.zh: 那个葡萄酒香气轮盘是安·诺布尔（Ann Noble）设计的。

sentences.en: She's an expert in both the chemistry and psychophysics of wine.
sentences.zh: 她是葡萄酒化学和心理物理学方面的专家。

sentences.en: She's retired now.
sentences.zh: 她现在已经退休了。

sentences.en: She's out in California.
sentences.zh: 她住在加利福尼亚。

sentences.en: And she's the one that put real science into a lot of that.
sentences.zh: 正是她将真正的科学引入了其中的许多领域。

sentences.en: Yeah, and it's very fascinating.
sentences.zh: 是啊，这非常迷人。

sentences.en: Like I said, I had no idea because I was thinking, you see these charts that say you can taste chalk or smoke in wine.
sentences.zh: 就像我说的，我以前完全不知道，因为我看到那些图表上写着酒里能尝出粉笔或烟熏味。

sentences.en: I'm like, how do, I guess we all know the smell of chalk from growing up or whatnot.
sentences.zh: 我在想，我们大概都知道从小到大闻到的粉笔味之类的东西。

sentences.en: But of all the things, like, yeah, you have to kind of re-sniff that to be able to identify that in a glass of wine.
sentences.zh: 但不管怎么说，你确实得重新去闻一下，才能在酒杯中识别出那种味道。

sentences.en: But I didn't realize if you're training yourself in that area that you should be smelling a lot of different things.
sentences.zh: 但我没意识到，如果你要在那个领域训练自己，你应该去闻各种各样的东西。

sentences.en: That is correct.
sentences.zh: 那是正确的。

sentences.en: And I want to talk about some of your research you've done.
sentences.zh: 我想谈谈你做过的一些研究。

sentences.en: You've been involved in work to enhance the flavor of tomatoes.
sentences.zh: 你曾参与过提升番茄风味的工作。

sentences.en: So why tomatoes?
sentences.zh: 那么，为什么要选番茄呢？

sentences.en: Well, we started with tomatoes because my colleague, Harry Klee, is one of the world's experts on tomato volatiles.
sentences.zh: 嗯，我们从番茄开始，因为我的同事哈里·克里（Harry Klee）是世界上番茄挥发性物质方面的专家之一。

sentences.en: And we began with the tomato because we wanted to make it more palatable.
sentences.zh: 我们从番茄入手，是因为我们想让它变得更可口。

sentences.en: Now, I don't know if you've eaten supermarket tomatoes recently, but they leave a lot to be desired.
sentences.zh: 我不知道你最近有没有吃过超市里的番茄，它们实在让人不敢恭维。

sentences.en: Most people have a memory of a tomato that was really wonderful and a lot better than what you can usually buy in the supermarket.
sentences.zh: 大多数人记忆中的番茄都非常美味，比你在超市里通常能买到的要好得多。

sentences.en: Well, part of the reason for that is that we have raised tomatoes to ship.
sentences.zh: 嗯，部分原因是我们将番茄培育成了适合运输的品种。

sentences.en: And if you want to breed tomatoes to have good shipping characteristics, you're not paying much attention to their flavor.
sentences.zh: 如果你想培育出具有良好运输特性的番茄，你就不会太在意它们的风味。

sentences.en: So Harry wanted to make tomatoes more palatable.
sentences.zh: 所以哈里想让番茄变得更可口。

sentences.en: And also, tomatoes are healthy.
sentences.zh: 而且，番茄很健康。

sentences.en: So if we make them more palatable, can we improve the diet by getting people to eat more of something like a tomato that's a healthy thing to eat?
sentences.zh: 所以如果我们让它们更可口，能不能通过让人们多吃像番茄这样健康的食物来改善饮食呢？

sentences.en: Well, it turns out it's not a very difficult problem.
sentences.zh: 嗯，事实证明这并不是一个太难的问题。

sentences.en: You really want to know what it is in the tomato that makes it light.
sentences.zh: 你确实需要知道番茄里到底是什么让它变得美味。

sentences.en: Well, you do the chemistry on the tomatoes.
sentences.zh: 嗯，你得对番茄进行化学分析。

sentences.en: And we actually grew at the University of Florida because we are a farm agricultural college, so we have farmland.
sentences.zh: 我们实际上是在佛罗里达大学种植的，因为我们是一所农业学院，所以我们有农田。

sentences.en: We grew our own tomatoes and we grew heirloom tomatoes.
sentences.zh: 我们种植了自己的番茄，也种植了传家宝番茄。

sentences.en: Now, heirloom tomatoes, people think heirlooms are better tomatoes.
sentences.zh: 现在，人们认为传家宝番茄是更好的番茄。

sentences.en: They're not.
sentences.zh: 其实不然。

sentences.en: Heirloom means they're genetically diverse.
sentences.zh: 传家宝意味着它们在基因上是多样的。

sentences.en: It refers to tomatoes that came before we started breeding them for shipping.
sentences.zh: 它指的是在我们开始为了运输而进行育种之前的那些番茄品种。

sentences.en: Anyway, we grew heirloom tomatoes because they're genetically diverse.
sentences.zh: 总之，我们种植传家宝番茄是因为它们具有基因多样性。

sentences.en: We did the chemistry on them.
sentences.zh: 我们对它们进行了化学分析。

sentences.en: And we did the psychophysics.
sentences.zh: 我们还进行了心理物理学测试。

sentences.en: We measured both what they tasted and smelled like and we measured how much people liked them.
sentences.zh: 我们既测量了它们的味道和气味，也测量了人们对它们的喜爱程度。

sentences.en: Turns out, you put all that together and you put it into a regression model, which we were helped with by our colleague, Howard Moskowitz.
sentences.zh: 事实证明，把所有这些数据汇总起来，放入一个回归模型中，我们的同事霍华德·莫斯科维茨（Howard Moskowitz）在这方面帮了我们大忙。

sentences.en: And this regression model actually will give you the formula for the great tomato.
sentences.zh: 这个回归模型实际上能给你提供完美番茄的配方。

sentences.en: Now, we could have created the best tomato in the world, but actually that's really, really hard to do because it requires a lot of chemistry.
sentences.zh: 我们本可以创造出世界上最好的番茄，但实际上这非常非常难，因为它需要大量的化学知识。

sentences.en: Anyway, what we did do is determine which constituents in the tomato contributed what to palatability so that we could create tomatoes that were better.
sentences.zh: 总之，我们所做的是确定番茄中的哪些成分对可口性有贡献，以便我们能创造出更好的番茄。

sentences.en: And actually, Harry Clee did create such a tomato.
sentences.zh: 事实上，哈里·克里确实创造出了这样一种番茄。

sentences.en: It's called a garden gem.
sentences.zh: 它被称为“花园宝石”（Garden Gem）。

sentences.en: And if you want to get seeds and grow that tomato, send him an email message and send a donation to his lab and I'll bet he'll give you some of his rare tomato seeds.
sentences.zh: 如果你想获得种子并种植那种番茄，给他发封电子邮件，并给他的实验室捐点款，我敢打赌他会给你一些他珍稀的番茄种子。

sentences.en: Anyway, why did we start with tomatoes?
sentences.zh: 总之，我们为什么从番茄开始？

sentences.en: Because they were there and it was easy.
sentences.zh: 因为它们就在那里，而且很容易处理。

sentences.en: But we've now done the same work with strawberries and oranges and peaches and blueberries.
sentences.zh: 但我们现在已经在草莓、橙子、桃子和蓝莓上做了同样的工作。

sentences.en: And we know a very, very great deal about which constituents in fruit make them liked better.
sentences.zh: 我们对水果中哪些成分能让它们更受欢迎有了非常非常深入的了解。

sentences.en: And we also know which volatiles in the fruit contribute to sweet.
sentences.zh: 我们也知道水果中哪些挥发性物质有助于产生甜味。

sentences.en: So it has more to do with transporting food than it is of the food itself.
sentences.zh: 所以这更多是关于食物的运输，而不是食物本身的问题。

sentences.en: So, you know, I definitely have tasted some very disappointing tomatoes at the grocery store or when I have grown some outside, they're incredibly delicious.
sentences.zh: 所以，你知道，我确实在杂货店尝过一些非常令人失望的番茄，或者当我自己在外面种了一些时，它们却美味得不可思议。

sentences.en: So it's fascinating that it's really based on consumer needs in the grocery store.
sentences.zh: 所以，它实际上是基于杂货店消费者的需求，这真令人着迷。

sentences.en: You know, the sad part about it is we've got the science to make almost anything we grow better.
sentences.zh: 你知道，可悲的是，我们已经掌握了让几乎所有我们种植的东西变得更好的科学技术。

sentences.en: What you need to do is understand the economics and you have to understand what the farmer is paid for and what he's going to grow.
sentences.zh: 你需要做的是了解经济学，了解农民靠什么赚钱，以及他打算种什么。

sentences.en: And unfortunately, a lot of farmers are paid for fruit or vegetables by wheat.
sentences.zh: 不幸的是，许多农民是按重量来出售水果或蔬菜的。

sentences.en: And we don't insist that they become – that they be very palatable.
sentences.zh: 我们并没有坚持要求它们必须——必须非常可口。

sentences.en: If we insist on that, the breeders and the growers can produce it.
sentences.zh: 如果我们坚持这一点，育种者和种植者是可以生产出来的。

sentences.en: We just have to insist on it.
sentences.zh: 我们只需要坚持要求就行了。

sentences.en: And those may be the ones you – they might be a little more ripe, so you might have to eat them more quickly.
sentences.zh: 而那些可能是你——它们可能成熟度更高，所以你可能得更快吃掉它们。

sentences.en: If you get them from the grocery store, that might come into play a little bit, correct?
sentences.zh: 如果你从杂货店买，这可能也会有点影响，对吧？

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: Yep.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: That's called post-harveSt.
sentences.zh: 这被称为采后处理。

sentences.en: That is how you treat something is going to affect its flavor as well as the genetics of the plant.
sentences.zh: 你对待事物的方式会影响它的风味，植物的遗传基因也是如此。

sentences.en: So you have to pay attention to all of it.
sentences.zh: 所以你必须关注所有这些方面。

sentences.en: Have you ever heard about how tomato juice tastes better on airplanes?
sentences.zh: 你有没有听说过番茄汁在飞机上喝起来味道更好？

sentences.en: Or people tend to order more V8 when they're on an airplane than they would on the ground?
sentences.zh: 或者人们在飞机上点V8蔬菜汁的频率比在地面上更高？

sentences.en: I've heard that.
sentences.zh: 我听说过。

sentences.en: And I know absolutely no good science that supports it.
sentences.zh: 而且我绝对不知道有什么好的科学证据支持这一点。

sentences.en: There are some papers on that, but they aren't very impressive.
sentences.zh: 有一些关于这方面的论文，但它们并不令人印象深刻。

sentences.en: Maybe I haven't read them all.
sentences.zh: 也许我还没读完所有的论文。

sentences.en: But this notion is – I know every so often it pops up online, and it is not something that is generally understood and believed in by experts.
sentences.zh: 但这个概念——我知道它时不时会在网上冒出来，但这并不是专家们普遍理解和相信的东西。

sentences.en: So it's maybe more of a placebo effect.
sentences.zh: 所以这可能更多是一种安慰剂效应。

sentences.en: I'm not sure what it is.
sentences.zh: 我不确定它到底是什么。

sentences.en: I shouldn't say absolutely it can't happen.
sentences.zh: 我不应该绝对地说它不可能发生。

sentences.en: There are – the same kinds of stories come from submarines.
sentences.zh: 有——同样的说法也来自潜艇。

sentences.en: The same things come from our astronauts.
sentences.zh: 同样的事情也来自我们的宇航员。

sentences.en: Do things taste different to them when they're in outer space?
sentences.zh: 当他们在太空中时，食物的味道对他们来说会改变吗？

sentences.en: Unfortunately, we haven't done a lot of research on that.
sentences.zh: 不幸的是，我们在这方面没有做过太多的研究。

sentences.en: But in fact, there's not a lot of really solid evidence for it.
sentences.zh: 但事实上，并没有多少真正可靠的证据支持这一点。

sentences.en: However, if anybody's got some evidence, I'm happy to look.
sentences.zh: 不过，如果有人有证据，我很乐意看看。

sentences.en: Yeah, that would be a new – open up some new areas of research too, like you said, if we're going into space, underground, that sort of thing.
sentences.zh: 是啊，那也会开启一些新的研究领域，就像你说的，如果我们进入太空、地下，诸如此类的地方。

sentences.en: Maybe it's also people are just ordering Bloody Marys or something on the – or they wish they had a Bloody Mary on the plane.
sentences.zh: 也许也只是因为人们在飞机上点了血腥玛丽（Bloody Mary），或者他们希望在飞机上能有一杯血腥玛丽。

sentences.en: Well, I think that most of the people who are getting tomato juice on the plane, I mean, they're probably getting alcohol in it.
sentences.zh: 嗯，我认为大多数在飞机上喝番茄汁的人，我的意思是，他们可能是在里面加了酒精。

sentences.en: That probably has a little bit to do with their judgment.
sentences.zh: 这可能对他们的判断力有一点影响。

sentences.en: Yeah, that could be true too.
sentences.zh: 是啊，那也可能是真的。

sentences.en: It tastes better.
sentences.zh: 味道更好。

sentences.en: For those experiments you're talking about with strawberries and oranges, is that because maybe strawberries are picked too soon?
sentences.zh: 对于你提到的那些关于草莓和橙子的实验，是因为草莓可能采摘得太早了吗？

sentences.en: Because when I thought of like an orange or a strawberry, I typically thought, you know, if you get them at the right time of year at the grocery store, they're pretty good.
sentences.zh: 因为当我想到橙子或草莓这类水果时，我通常会想，如果你能在一年中合适的季节去杂货店买，它们味道还是相当不错的。

sentences.en: But is the same concern there with, you know, we're focusing on asking farmers to give it to us by weight and we're worried about shipping.
sentences.zh: 但我们是否也存在同样的顾虑，比如我们专注于要求农民按重量供应，而我们又担心运输问题？

sentences.en: We're not concerned about the taste.
sentences.zh: 我们并不关心味道。

sentences.en: There's a lot of interest in making good things, making strawberries good.
sentences.zh: 人们对制造好东西、让草莓变得美味有很大的兴趣。

sentences.en: And wow, we know a lot about that now because we know which volatiles in the strawberries make them sweeter.
sentences.zh: 哇，我们现在对此了解很多，因为我们知道草莓中的哪些挥发性物质能让它们更甜。

sentences.en: And in fact, there are about 30 some volatiles in a tomato that all add a little bit of sweetness to it because those volatiles, when we bite into the strawberry,
sentences.zh: 事实上，番茄中大约有30多种挥发性物质，它们都能增加一点甜味，因为当我们咬下草莓时，这些挥发性物质，

sentences.en: travel – the message travels to the same part of the brain that codes for the sweetness of sugar.
sentences.zh: 会传递信息——信息会传到大脑中负责编码糖分甜度的同一区域。

sentences.en: And those volatiles enhance the sweetness message in the brain.
sentences.zh: 而这些挥发性物质增强了大脑中的甜味信号。

sentences.en: Now, once you've identified those volatiles, you can take them out of the strawberry and put them in pure sugar and it'll get sweeter.
sentences.zh: 现在，一旦你确定了这些挥发性物质，你就可以把它们从草莓中提取出来，加入纯糖中，它就会变得更甜。

sentences.en: So, this is one of the things I'm very excited about right now because it looks like about the safest way to make a so-called artificial sweet that could possibly exiSt.
sentences.zh: 所以，这是我现在非常兴奋的事情之一，因为它看起来是目前可能存在的最安全的所谓人工甜味剂的制作方式。

sentences.en: We use volatiles that we've already been eating ever since humans were humans.
sentences.zh: 我们使用的是人类自诞生以来就一直在食用的挥发性物质。

sentences.en: And they're going to – if you pick the right volatiles, they're going to produce sweetness in the brain.
sentences.zh: 而且它们会——如果你选择了正确的挥发性物质，它们就会在大脑中产生甜味。

sentences.en: Now, first of all, you can certainly breed for those volatiles in the strawberry and you're going to produce strawberries that do not need any sugar.
sentences.zh: 首先，你当然可以通过培育草莓来获得这些挥发性物质，这样你生产出的草莓就不需要任何糖分了。

sentences.en: I have tasted some of these strawberries and I'm telling you, when they're widely available, people are really going to like them.
sentences.zh: 我尝过一些这样的草莓，我敢说，当它们广泛上市时，人们一定会非常喜欢。

sentences.en: But at the same time, we can put these volatiles in anything that we want to be sweeter and we can make it sweeter safely for, let's say, diabetics.
sentences.zh: 但与此同时，我们可以把这些挥发性物质添加到任何我们想要增加甜度的东西中，这样我们就可以安全地让它变甜，比如为糖尿病患者提供选择。

sentences.en: But there's something else about it that I'm very excited about.
sentences.zh: 但关于这一点，还有另一件事让我非常兴奋。

sentences.en: I've spent a lot of my career studying people who have taste damage.
sentences.zh: 我的职业生涯中花了很多时间研究味觉受损的人群。

sentences.en: And one of the things about using volatiles to affect a taste message in the brain is those volatiles bypass damaged nerves.
sentences.zh: 利用挥发性物质来影响大脑中的味觉信号，其中一个特点就是这些挥发性物质可以绕过受损的神经。

sentences.en: That is, if your taste nerve is damaged, you can't perceive more sweet from sugar because you don't have the nerve to carry the message.
sentences.zh: 也就是说，如果你的味觉神经受损，你就无法从糖中感知到更多的甜味，因为你没有神经来传递这个信息。

sentences.en: But if you consume sugar that has some of these volatiles in that enhance sweet, those are going to – the volatiles,
sentences.zh: 但如果你食用的糖中含有一些能增强甜味的挥发性物质，那么这些挥发性物质，

sentences.en: the message is going to bypass the damaged nerve and increase the sweet message in the brain.
sentences.zh: 信息就会绕过受损的神经，增加大脑中的甜味信号。

sentences.en: And I'm happy to say that the early test with patients supports this.
sentences.zh: 我很高兴地说，早期的患者测试支持了这一点。

sentences.en: It looks like it's going to work.
sentences.zh: 看起来这确实有效。

sentences.en: Would those enhancements be considered genetically modified?
sentences.zh: 这些增强效果会被认为是基因改造吗？

sentences.en: No, no.
sentences.zh: 不，不。

sentences.en: Organisms?
sentences.zh: 生物体？

sentences.en: Okay.
sentences.zh: 好的。

sentences.en: Nobody does that today.
sentences.zh: 今天没人会那样做。

sentences.en: Well, not nobody.
sentences.zh: 嗯，也不是完全没人。

sentences.en: But the fact is there's so much prejudice against genetic modified.
sentences.zh: 但事实是，人们对基因改造存在太多的偏见。

sentences.en: And I have to tell you, I'm not a supporter of that prejudice.
sentences.zh: 我必须告诉你，我并不支持这种偏见。

sentences.en: If we want to feed the world, we want to use the best science we've got.
sentences.zh: 如果我们想养活全世界，我们就应该利用我们所拥有的最好的科学。

sentences.en: And if we can genetically modify something to make it – put up, say, a vitamin in rice that's going to save children in the third world from going blind, I say all for it.
sentences.zh: 如果我们能通过基因改造来让某种东西——比如在稻米中加入维生素，从而拯救第三世界的儿童免于失明，我完全支持。

sentences.en: And I know of no evidence that genetically modified organisms are in any way dangerous.
sentences.zh: 而且我不知道有任何证据表明基因改造生物在任何方面是危险的。

sentences.en: I think that's a type of prejudice that's gotten into the world.
sentences.zh: 我认为这是一种已经渗透到世界各地的偏见。

sentences.en: I don't know how it got there, and I'm sorry it's there because I think it's doing a lot of harm.
sentences.zh: 我不知道它是怎么产生的，我很遗憾它存在，因为我认为它造成了很大的伤害。

sentences.en: Yeah, definitely.
sentences.zh: 是的，确实如此。

sentences.en: I mean, there's a lot of arguments against it, but I've heard more than one person say your side of it, and typically someone who's a researcher in the science field, saying, like,
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，反对它的论点很多，但我听过不止一个人说出你的观点，通常是科学领域的研究人员，他们会说，

sentences.en: if we can feed people out there who otherwise wouldn't be able to get the nutrition they need, then we need to think about that.
sentences.zh: 如果我们能养活那些原本无法获得所需营养的人，那么我们就需要考虑这一点。

sentences.en: We sure do.
sentences.zh: 我们当然需要。

sentences.en: And also, I wanted to touch on your burning mouth syndrome.
sentences.zh: 另外，我还想谈谈你的灼口综合征。

sentences.en: So I'm sure most people who are listening have all burned their mouths on food and know how annoying it is.
sentences.zh: 我相信大多数听众都曾因食物烫伤过口腔，知道那有多烦人。

sentences.en: Your tongue goes numb and nothing really tastes great for a couple days.
sentences.zh: 你的舌头会麻木，接下来的几天里吃什么都没味道。

sentences.en: But for some people, that doesn't go away.
sentences.zh: 但对有些人来说，这种感觉不会消失。

sentences.en: And so your lab uncovered the reasons why people suffer from this.
sentences.zh: 所以你的实验室揭示了人们患此病的原因。

sentences.en: So can you explain what the causes of burning mouth syndrome are and how many people might have it and how it can be treated?
sentences.zh: 那么你能解释一下灼口综合征的成因、有多少人可能患有此病以及如何治疗吗？

sentences.en: Burning mouth syndrome actually has nothing to do with damage in the mouth.
sentences.zh: 灼口综合征实际上与口腔损伤无关。

sentences.en: Burning mouth syndrome occurs in the brain.
sentences.zh: 灼口综合征发生在大脑中。

sentences.en: It's what we call a sensory phantom.
sentences.zh: 这就是我们所说的感觉幻觉。

sentences.en: You can make a phantom in any sensory nerve in the body.
sentences.zh: 你可以在身体的任何感觉神经中制造幻觉。

sentences.en: Have you ever heard of a phantom limb?
sentences.zh: 你听说过幻肢痛吗？

sentences.en: Yes.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: This is feeling.
sentences.zh: 这就是那种感觉。

sentences.en: An arm is there after it's been amputated.
sentences.zh: 手臂被截肢后，感觉它还在那里。

sentences.en: Well, you can have a phantom smell, a phantom taste, and a phantom pain in your tongue.
sentences.zh: 同样，你可能会有幻嗅、幻味，以及舌头上的幻痛。

sentences.en: So how does it happen?
sentences.zh: 那么它是怎么发生的呢？

sentences.en: We think what causes it is, believe it or not, damage to the taste nerve, the seventh cranial nerve.
