sentences.zh: 我们认为导致它的原因是，信不信由你，味觉神经，即第七对脑神经的损伤。

sentences.en: That nerve normally has two jobs.
sentences.zh: 那条神经通常有两个工作。

sentences.en: It both brings taste information to the brain, but it also terminates oral pain, maybe even pain on other parts of the body.
sentences.zh: 它既能把味觉信息传给大脑，也能终止口腔疼痛，甚至可能是身体其他部位的疼痛。

sentences.en: Now think about why that might be a good idea.
sentences.zh: 现在想想为什么这可能是一个好主意。

sentences.en: Imagine an animal in the wild fighting to survive with its teeth.
sentences.zh: 想象一下野外的一只动物，为了生存而用牙齿搏斗。

sentences.en: It's going to get bitten on some occasions, and another animal might bite it.
sentences.zh: 它有时会被咬伤，其他动物可能会咬它。

sentences.en: It might bite its own tongue.
sentences.zh: 它可能会咬伤自己的舌头。

sentences.en: And if tongue pain stops it from eating, an animal is going to die.
sentences.zh: 如果舌头疼痛阻止它进食，动物就会死亡。

sentences.en: So a survival characteristic would be to somehow stop the pain of any kind of oral damage.
sentences.zh: 所以一种生存特征就是以某种方式阻止任何口腔损伤带来的疼痛。

sentences.en: Well, if the animal takes a bite of food, and the food input, the sensory input, inhibits the pain, it's going to eat and survive.
sentences.zh: 好吧，如果动物咬了一口食物，食物的输入，即感觉输入，抑制了疼痛，它就能进食并生存下来。

sentences.en: It looks like that mechanism connected the taste system to pain.
sentences.zh: 看起来这种机制将味觉系统与疼痛联系在了一起。

sentences.en: So what happens is, if you damage taste, you lose the ability of taste to inhibit pain.
sentences.zh: 所以发生的情况是，如果你损伤了味觉，你就失去了味觉抑制疼痛的能力。

sentences.en: And essentially, pain turns on in the brain.
sentences.zh: 本质上，疼痛在大脑中被开启了。

sentences.en: It's like you flipped a switch, and you can't reach it to turn it off.
sentences.zh: 就像你按下了开关，却无法触及它来关闭它。

sentences.en: Now, how can you get rid of the phantom?
sentences.zh: 那么，你该如何摆脱这种幻觉呢？

sentences.en: And by the way, let me tell you how we discovered that the phantom was in the brain.
sentences.zh: 顺便说一下，让我告诉你我们是如何发现这种幻觉发生在大脑中的。

sentences.en: If you had a burnt mouth, it would be easy to treat it.
sentences.zh: 如果你真的烫伤了嘴，治疗起来会很容易。

sentences.en: All you'd have to do is anesthetize the area of the burn, and the pain would go away.
sentences.zh: 你只需要对烫伤区域进行麻醉，疼痛就会消失。

sentences.en: When we anesthetize the tongues of people with burning mouth syndrome, the burn gets worse.
sentences.zh: 当我们对灼口综合征患者的舌头进行麻醉时，灼烧感反而加重了。

sentences.en: Why does it get worse?
sentences.zh: 为什么会加重呢？

sentences.en: Because the burn is only occurring in people with damage to taste.
sentences.zh: 因为这种灼烧感只发生在味觉受损的人身上。

sentences.en: And when we anesthetize their tongues, we take out whatever taste was left, and we make the effects of the damage worse.
sentences.zh: 当我们麻醉他们的舌头时，我们去掉了仅存的味觉，从而加剧了损伤的影响。

sentences.en: So the pain phantom in the brain gets worse.
sentences.zh: 所以大脑中的疼痛幻觉就加重了。

sentences.en: Now, that goes away when the anesthetic wears off, fortunately.
sentences.zh: 幸运的是，当麻醉药效消失后，这种疼痛就会消失。

sentences.en: But you don't have just burn phantoms in the mouth.
sentences.zh: 但口腔中不仅仅有灼烧幻觉。

sentences.en: You can have taste phantoms, and you can have touch phantoMs.
sentences.zh: 你还可能有味觉幻觉和触觉幻觉。

sentences.en: For example, you could wake up one morning with a bitter taste in your mouth that never went away.
sentences.zh: 例如，你可能某天早上醒来，嘴里有一种挥之不去的苦味。

sentences.en: Believe me, you would not be happy.
sentences.zh: 相信我，你不会开心的。

sentences.en: And so, can it be treated?
sentences.zh: 那么，它能被治疗吗？

sentences.en: Yes, it can.
sentences.zh: 是的，可以。

sentences.en: And I can tell you, one of the reasons that I got so interested in this was my father had lung cancer when I was in college,
sentences.zh: 我可以告诉你，我对此产生浓厚兴趣的原因之一是我父亲在大学时患了肺癌，

sentences.en: and his most distressing symptom was a metallic taste in his mouth that wouldn't go away.
sentences.zh: 他最痛苦的症状就是嘴里有一种挥之不去的金属味。

sentences.en: And we didn't know what to do for him at that time, but one of the reasons I got interested in phantoms was to try to figure out how to help patients.
sentences.zh: 当时我们不知道该怎么帮他，但我对幻觉产生兴趣的原因之一，就是想找出如何帮助患者的方法。

sentences.en: It turns out we can use a medication that intensifies inhibitory neurotransmitters in the brain.
sentences.zh: 事实证明，我们可以使用一种能增强大脑中抑制性神经递质的药物。

sentences.en: It's called a GABA agonist, and a GABA agonist will restore some of that inhibition from taste that was lost from damage, and it will reduce that burn phantom in about 60%,
sentences.zh: 它被称为GABA激动剂，GABA激动剂可以恢复一些因损伤而丧失的味觉抑制作用，并能减轻约60%到

sentences.en: 70% of patients.
sentences.zh: 70%患者的灼烧幻觉。

sentences.en: And I can't take the credit for that.
sentences.zh: 这功劳我可不敢独占。

sentences.en: That was discovered by Dr. Miriam Grushka, who is an oral pathology expert.
sentences.zh: 这是由口腔病理学专家Miriam Grushka博士发现的。

sentences.en: Yeah, it sounds like a really troubling situation that can happen, but it's nice to know there's at least a solution for people, like I said,
sentences.zh: 是的，这听起来确实是一个非常令人困扰的情况，但很高兴知道至少有一种解决方案，就像我说的，

sentences.en: not just me burning my mouth, having a metallic taste, because that really can inhibit the quality of your life if you have a bad taste in your mouth all the time.
sentences.zh: 不仅仅是我烫伤了嘴，那种金属味真的会严重影响你的生活质量，如果你一直觉得嘴里有怪味的话。

sentences.en: It is awful.
sentences.zh: 这太糟糕了。

sentences.en: It's one of the reasons why that's the specialty area that I work on in taste pathology, because it probably produces more distress for patients than any other taste problem.
sentences.zh: 这就是我从事味觉病理学这一专业领域的原因之一，因为它给患者带来的痛苦可能比任何其他味觉问题都要大。

sentences.en: Yeah, because the quality of life, the enjoyment of food, it's just everything.
sentences.zh: 是的，因为生活质量，对食物的享受，这简直是一切。

sentences.en: I mean, you're living with that every second of every day of just having a disturbing taste in your mouth.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，你每天每秒都要忍受嘴里那种令人不安的味道。

sentences.en: Well, thank you so much for joining us, Dr. Bartosz.
sentences.zh: 非常感谢您参加我们的节目，Bartosz博士。

sentences.en: This has been a really fascinating conversation,
sentences.zh: 这是一次非常引人入胜的谈话，

sentences.en: and I'm probably going to head out to the grocery store and get some of that blue dye and test out that experiment you mentioned earlier today.
sentences.zh: 我可能要去杂货店买点那种蓝色染料，试试你今天早些时候提到的那个实验。

sentences.en: That sounds like a lot of fun.
sentences.zh: 听起来很有趣。

sentences.en: Do you do that at parties?
sentences.zh: 你在聚会上也做这个吗？

sentences.en: You know, the truth is I actually have done it at lectures.
sentences.zh: 老实说，我确实在讲座上做过。

sentences.en: I take paper with me that is bitter to supertasters and pick the people in the audience who think the paper is just awful and put blue food coloring on and let everybody look at their tongue.
sentences.zh: 我随身带着对超级味觉者来说很苦的纸，挑选出观众中觉得纸味道极其糟糕的人，给他们的舌头涂上蓝色食用色素，让大家看看他们的舌头。

sentences.en: That's a lot of fun.
sentences.zh: 那真的很有趣。

sentences.en: That's a really great idea.
sentences.zh: 那真是个好主意。

sentences.en: Good thing to do with kids.
sentences.zh: 很适合和孩子们一起做。

sentences.en: But thanks again so much for your time.
sentences.zh: 再次非常感谢你抽出时间。

sentences.en: It's been a real pleasure speaking with you.
sentences.zh: 和你交谈真是太愉快了。

sentences.en: I'm delighted.
sentences.zh: 我很高兴。

sentences.en: And thank you for being so well prepared.
sentences.zh: 也谢谢你准备得如此充分。

sentences.en: I really enjoyed this.
sentences.zh: 我真的很享受这次谈话。

sentences.en: Before we go, just a reminder to let you know we want to hear from you.
sentences.zh: 在结束之前，提醒大家，我们很想听到你们的声音。

sentences.zh: That's K-L-U-N-A at apa.org.
